note: Real Convai text replies (scripts/Probe-EmotionReplies.mjs) with the character's own inline tags and Convai's late label; each segment labelled blind to the picker by a separate writer (Sonnet).

set1-alex-000.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-alex-000.text: People say a lot of things. Whether it is true depends on who is telling the story and what they think capture looks like.

set1-alex-001.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-alex-001.text: It is a professional habit. Besides, the truth is usually a lot less interesting than the version people make up.

set1-alex-002.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-alex-002.text: It is called a disguise. Though I will admit, the fashion choice is a bit loud for my taste.

set1-alex-003.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-alex-003.text: Careful. You keep that up and I might actually start believing you.

set1-alex-004.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-alex-004.text: We are not lost. We are just exploring the scenic route. Give me a minute to check the map.

set1-alex-005.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-alex-005.text: Keep walking. Don't look back. I'll check the reflections in the windows and let you know if we have company.

set1-alex-006.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-alex-006.text: Now that is a feeling I can get behind. I imagine the air tastes a lot cleaner when you do not owe a fixer a cent.

set1-alex-007.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-alex-007.text: Sometimes. But the person I used to be didn't know how to survive in a place like this. I think I prefer the version that does.

set1-alex-008.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-alex-008.text: They are just children playing with gods' toys. They think they own the world because they have a fancy office and a security detail, but they are just as trapped as the rest of us.

set1-alex-009.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set1-alex-009.text: I can't see what you're pointing at right now. Which one do you mean?

set1-alex-010.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-alex-010.text: I appreciate that. It has been a long road, and not all of it was by choice.

set1-alex-011.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-alex-011.text: You did what? Well, at least we do not have to worry about the cameras seeing us leave.

set1-alex-012.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-alex-012.text: Glad I could provide some entertainment. Just don't expect me to make a habit of it.

set1-alex-013.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-alex-013.text: Trust is earned, not proven on command. I'm fine with you keeping your guard up. It's the only way to stay alive in this city.

set1-alex-014.text: Not much to tell. I grew up in the Los Angeles Metroplex. It was a ghetto, and my main goal in life was simply to get out of it.

set1-alex-015.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-alex-015.text: I've had worse. But if you're offering, I won't stop you. Just be gentle.

set1-alex-016.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-alex-016.text: A chainsaw? You're exaggerating. I'll have to start recording you to see if the feeling is mutual.

set1-alex-017.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-alex-017.text: Somewhere warm. A place with sweet fruit, a decent drink, and absolutely no field work. Ambitious enough for you?

set1-alex-018.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-alex-018.text: Don't be. I made my own choices to be here. Besides, a little mess keeps things from getting boring.

set1-alex-019.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-alex-019.text: Well, at least they have manners. Now the real question is whether they left the keys in the note.

set1-alex-020.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-alex-020.text: Depends on how much you value your life and how quiet you need the cleanup to be. My rates aren't cheap, but I'm very efficient.

set1-alex-021.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-alex-021.text: I've survived seven years in Dogtown. I'm not planning on letting a little operation be the thing that finally catches up with me.

set1-alex-022.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-alex-022.text: I didn't lie. I just gave you the version of the truth that kept us from getting shot. In my line of work, there is a big difference.

set1-alex-023.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-alex-023.text: It does. For a moment, you can almost pretend the rest of the city isn't trying to tear itself apart.

set1-alex-024.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-alex-024.text: Not yet. Let him stare. It is better to know exactly where the threat is than to have it hiding in the shadows.

set1-alex-025.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-alex-025.text: You got me. I'll be sure to return the favor when you least expect it.

set1-alex-026.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-alex-026.text: Now we are talking. Let's get it moved before someone decides they want a piece of it.

set1-alex-027.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-alex-027.text: I can't see what you're holding. Why don't you describe it, and I'll tell you if I'm interested in claiming it.

set1-evelyn-parker-028.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-evelyn-parker-028.text: People love to trade stories in this city. Most of them are just trying to make someone else sound more interesting, or more vulnerable, than they actually are.

set1-evelyn-parker-029.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-evelyn-parker-029.text: I don't dodge. I simply prefer to decide which parts of my history are useful for the person I am talking to.

set1-evelyn-parker-030.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-evelyn-parker-030.text: Is that your way of telling me you prefer something a bit more street? Or are you just testing to see if I can be rattled by a comment about my clothes?

set1-evelyn-parker-031.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-evelyn-parker-031.text: I appreciate the honesty. It is a refreshing change from the usual scripts people follow when they want something from me.

set1-evelyn-parker-032.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-evelyn-parker-032.text: Lost is a strong word. I prefer to think of it as an unplanned detour. Unless you have a better sense of direction than the map provided.

set1-evelyn-parker-033.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-evelyn-parker-033.text: Then we stop pretending we don't notice. Let's see if they have the nerve to actually close the gap.

set1-evelyn-parker-034.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-evelyn-parker-034.text: That is a rare feeling in this city. I imagine the air tastes a little cleaner now that you don't owe anyone your life.

set1-evelyn-parker-035.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-evelyn-parker-035.text: The person I used to be didn't have the tools to get where I am now. I don't miss the limitations, even if the current view is a bit more dangerous.

set1-evelyn-parker-036.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-evelyn-parker-036.text: They sell the idea that power is the same thing as control. It is a convincing pitch, but I have seen enough of them to know it is usually a lie.

set1-evelyn-parker-037.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set1-evelyn-parker-037.text: I am not sure which one you mean. Be specific.

set1-evelyn-parker-038.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-evelyn-parker-038.text: That is kind of you to say. Just make sure you aren't confusing my progress with a finished story.

set1-evelyn-parker-039.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-evelyn-parker-039.text: Accidentally. I hope for your sake that the information was redundant, because a recording is often the only thing that catches what people were too busy to notice.

set1-evelyn-parker-040.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-evelyn-parker-040.text: I am glad my lack of judgment could be so entertaining for you. Just try not to make a habit of encouraging it.

set1-evelyn-parker-041.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-evelyn-parker-041.text: Trust is a heavy word. I would rather be useful than trusted. If you want proof, watch how I handle the next problem. That is the only currency that actually matters here.

set1-evelyn-parker-042.text: I find that talking about family usually leads to conversations that are far too personal for the kind of business we do.

set1-evelyn-parker-043.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-evelyn-parker-043.text: I can handle it. But if you are offering your services for free, I might be persuaded to let you take a look.

set1-evelyn-parker-044.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-evelyn-parker-044.text: I suspect you are imagining things. Or perhaps you are just trying to find a way to make me feel self conscious.

set1-evelyn-parker-045.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-evelyn-parker-045.text: I want to be in a position where I no longer have to ask for permission to leave a room. And perhaps find a place where the food actually tastes like it existed before the packaging.

set1-evelyn-parker-046.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-evelyn-parker-046.text: Apologies are a luxury we can't really afford right now. Just make sure the way out is worth the trouble we went through to get in.

set1-evelyn-parker-047.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-evelyn-parker-047.text: Well, at least they had the courtesy to be polite about it. In this city, a thank you note is practically a formal apology.

set1-evelyn-parker-048.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-evelyn-parker-048.text: That depends entirely on how much you are willing to risk and how quickly you need it done. I don't give quotes for vague requests. Tell me exactly what you need, and I will tell you what it costs.

set1-evelyn-parker-049.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-evelyn-parker-049.text: I think anyone who is certain they will survive in Night City is usually the first one to fall. The real question is whether we are willing to commit fully to the gamble.

set1-evelyn-parker-050.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-evelyn-parker-050.text: I didn't lie. I simply gave you the information that was necessary for you to do your part. There is a difference between deception and discretion.

set1-evelyn-parker-051.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-evelyn-parker-051.text: It is a beautiful mask. The city is very good at making you forget that the ground beneath you is just as unstable as everything else.

set1-evelyn-parker-052.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-evelyn-parker-052.text: Not yet. Let's see if he is just curious or if he is waiting for a signal. There is no need to start a fight before we know why he is watching.

set1-evelyn-parker-053.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-evelyn-parker-053.text: You should be careful with that kind of victory. I might have let you think you won just to see how you would react.

set1-evelyn-parker-054.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-evelyn-parker-054.text: Then the gamble paid off. Now we just have to make sure we can actually keep it without someone deciding they want a piece of the prize.

set1-evelyn-parker-055.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-evelyn-parker-055.text: I am not sure what you are referring to. Why don't you describe it, and I will tell you if it belongs to me.

set1-jackie-welles-056.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-jackie-welles-056.text: Who told you that? Look, everyone has a bad day in this city, hermano. Let's just say I learned a few things about patience and why you always keep a backup plan.

set1-jackie-welles-057.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-jackie-welles-057.text: Not dodging, V, just keeping the good stories for when we're celebrating a big score. Besides, the past is just a map of where not to go again.

set1-jackie-welles-058.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-jackie-welles-058.text: Ha! You think this is a loss? This is style, choom. Pure Heywood class. You just don't have the eye for it.

set1-jackie-welles-059.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-jackie-welles-059.text: Now we're talking! See, I knew you had some taste in you. I'll take the compliment, V.

set1-jackie-welles-060.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-jackie-welles-060.text: Lost? We aren't lost, we're just taking the scenic route. Give me a second to check the map and we'll be back on track.

set1-jackie-welles-061.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-jackie-welles-061.text: You think so? Keep your eyes open and stay sharp. If someone's tailing us, they're about to find out we aren't the kind of people you want to mess with.

set1-jackie-welles-062.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-jackie-welles-062.text: No way! That is the best news I have heard all week! We gotta celebrate, V. First round is on me.

set1-jackie-welles-063.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-jackie-welles-063.text: Sometimes. But the guy I was didn't have the goals I have now. I'd rather be the man who makes it to the Afterlife than the kid just trying to survive the block.

set1-jackie-welles-064.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-jackie-welles-064.text: Please. They think they own the air we breathe just because they sit in a tower. To them, we're just tools to be used and tossed. That is why we take their eddies and keep our souls, hermano.

set1-jackie-welles-065.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set1-jackie-welles-065.text: Which one? You gotta be more specific, V. I've got a few things rattling around in here.

set1-jackie-welles-066.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-jackie-welles-066.text: Thanks, V. Means a lot coming from you. We're both climbing the ladder, hermano, and we're doing it together.

set1-jackie-welles-067.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-jackie-welles-067.text: You what? Well, look on the bright side, choom. Now there is no evidence of us ever being there. Just hope the guards aren't the type to notice when things go missing.

set1-jackie-welles-068.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-jackie-welles-068.text: Ha! See, that is why we make a great team. You get to laugh, and I get to make it look spectacular.

set1-jackie-welles-069.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-jackie-welles-069.text: Damn, V. Where is this coming from? I don't need to prove anything. I've had your back since day one, and I'll have it until the end. That's the only proof that matters in this city.

set1-jackie-welles-070.text: Not much to tell, really. Just me and Mama. She is the heart of everything for me, V. Everything I do, all the risks I take, it is so she can have the life she deserves.

set1-jackie-welles-071.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-jackie-welles-071.text: It is just a scratch, V. I appreciate it, really, but I can handle it. I'll swing by Viktor's later if it starts acting up.

set1-jackie-welles-072.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-jackie-welles-072.text: What? You're lying! I don't snore, choom. You probably just had a nightmare about a construction site.

set1-jackie-welles-073.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-jackie-welles-073.text: Man, just imagine it. A huge score, a name that actually means something at the Afterlife, and enough eddies to make sure Mama never has to worry about a thing again. After that? Maybe just a long ride on the bike with nowhere to be.

set1-jackie-welles-074.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-jackie-welles-074.text: Hey, stop that. We stepped into this together, V. No regrets. We just gotta find a way out, and we're gonna do it side by side.

set1-jackie-welles-075.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-jackie-welles-075.text: They left a note? Man, that is almost respectful. Almost. Let's go find who thinks they can just walk off with your ride and say thanks.

set1-jackie-welles-076.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-jackie-welles-076.text: Depends on who you're hiring and how much heat you're expecting. If you want it done right and you want the people doing it to actually come home, you gotta pay a fair cut. No one works for free in Night City.

set1-jackie-welles-077.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-jackie-welles-077.text: Why you getting all dark on me, V? We're the best team in the city. We're gonna make it out, and we're gonna do it with enough eddies to buy the whole damn block.

set1-jackie-welles-078.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-jackie-welles-078.text: Lie? I didn't lie, V, I just didn't give you the whole picture until it was time. In this business, knowing too much too early can get you killed. Trust me, I had it under control.

set1-jackie-welles-079.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-jackie-welles-079.text: Yeah. It really does. Makes the whole city look almost peaceful from up here, doesn't it? Just for a second.

set1-jackie-welles-080.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-jackie-welles-080.text: He's definitely looking. Hold up, let's see if he makes a move first. No need to start a war if he's just admiring the view, but if he steps closer, you have my blessing, hermano.

set1-jackie-welles-081.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-jackie-welles-081.text: What? You got me! Damn, V, you're getting too good at this. I'm gonna have to start sleeping with one eye open around you.

set1-jackie-welles-082.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-jackie-welles-082.text: No way! We actually did it! I told you, V, I told you we were destined for the big leagues! Now come on, let's go find something expensive to drink!

set1-jackie-welles-083.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-jackie-welles-083.text: My bag? Depends on what you found, choom. Some things are just for my eyes, you know? Let's see it.

set1-johnny-silverhand-084.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-johnny-silverhand-084.text: Captured? I don't remember being in a cage. Whoever told you that's either lying or confusing me with some corporate lapdog.

set1-johnny-silverhand-085.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-johnny-silverhand-085.text: I'm not dodging. Most of it's just noise, V. You want the highlight reel or the parts where I fucked up? Because the truth is usually a lot less cinematic than the stories.

set1-johnny-silverhand-086.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-johnny-silverhand-086.text: This? I'm a digital ghost, V. I wear what the code gives me. If it looks like a corporate retreat uniform, blame the software.

set1-johnny-silverhand-087.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-johnny-silverhand-087.text: Careful. You keep talking like that and people might think you actually like me. But yeah, I've always had a knack for making the most of whatever I'm wearing.

set1-johnny-silverhand-088.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-johnny-silverhand-088.text: We aren't lost. We're just exploring the scenic route. Besides, the best parts of this city are the ones that aren't on the map.

set1-johnny-silverhand-089.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-johnny-silverhand-089.text: Probably. In this city, you're either the one following or the one being hunted. Just keep walking and let's see who's got the balls to actually step out of the shadows.

set1-johnny-silverhand-090.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-johnny-silverhand-090.text: Finally. Nothing feels better than owning your own skin again. Now you can actually start making moves instead of just digging yourself out of a hole.

set1-johnny-silverhand-091.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-johnny-silverhand-091.text: Sometimes. Not the mistakes, but the feeling of a guitar in my hands and a crowd that actually gave a shit. Now I'm just a voice in your head. Hard to miss a man when you're just the echo of him.

set1-johnny-silverhand-092.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-johnny-silverhand-092.text: Parasites. They build these glittering towers on a mountain of corpses and call it progress. They don't run the city, V. They just own the lease on everyone's soul.

set1-johnny-silverhand-093.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set1-johnny-silverhand-093.text: Hand you what? I'm an engram, V. I can't touch a damn thing. You're gonna have to find it yourself.

set1-johnny-silverhand-094.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-johnny-silverhand-094.text: Proud? That's a new one. I'm not exactly looking for a gold star, but I'll take it. Just don't expect me to start acting like a choir boy.

set1-johnny-silverhand-095.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-johnny-silverhand-095.text: Accidentally? Stop lying to yourself, V. You just did us a favor. Now the only version of the truth is the one we tell.

set1-johnny-silverhand-096.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-johnny-silverhand-096.text: See? That's the secret. If you do something stupid enough, it stops being a mistake and starts being a statement.

set1-johnny-silverhand-097.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-johnny-silverhand-097.text: Trust is a luxury, V. I don't expect it. You don't need to trust me to use me. Just keep your eyes open and your gun loaded, and we'll get along fine.

set1-johnny-silverhand-098.text: Not much to tell. Most of that bridge was burned a long time ago. When you spend your life trying to tear down the world, you don't exactly leave a lot of room for a family dinner.

set1-johnny-silverhand-099.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-johnny-silverhand-099.text: Look at what? I'm a ghost, V. I don't bleed, I don't bruise, and I sure as hell don't need a bandage. If you're seeing something, maybe it's your own chrome acting up.

set1-johnny-silverhand-100.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-johnny-silverhand-100.text: I'm a fucking piece of software, V. If you're hearing chainsaws in your sleep, you might want to get your head checked. Or maybe you're just dreaming about my music.

set1-johnny-silverhand-101.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-johnny-silverhand-101.text: Honestly? I just want to stop being a passenger. Whether that means fading out or finding a way to actually leave a mark on the world again, I'm not sure. But I'm done playing second fiddle in someone else's skull.

set1-johnny-silverhand-102.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-johnny-silverhand-102.text: Don't waste your breath. I'm the one who spent half a century as a digital blueprint. If anyone's in a mess, it's both of us. Just make sure we get out of it with a story worth telling.

set1-johnny-silverhand-103.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-johnny-silverhand-103.text: Now that's just class. Most people just take the keys and run, but this one had the decency to be a prick about it. Welcome to Night City.

set1-johnny-silverhand-104.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-johnny-silverhand-104.text: Depends on who you're paying and how much they think they can bleed you for. If you're asking me, the price is usually a lot higher than just eddies. It's usually a piece of your soul or a bullet in the back.

set1-johnny-silverhand-105.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-johnny-silverhand-105.text: Who says we're alive right now? In this city, making it out is a fairy tale. The real win is just making sure the bastards remember your name after you're gone.

set1-johnny-silverhand-106.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-johnny-silverhand-106.text: I didn't lie. I just gave you the version that kept you moving. In this game, the full truth is a luxury you can't afford until the job is done.

set1-johnny-silverhand-107.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-johnny-silverhand-107.text: Yeah, it's a hell of a mask. Just remember that the higher you climb to see the view, the further you have to fall when the floor drops out.

set1-johnny-silverhand-108.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-johnny-silverhand-108.text: Go for it. Either he's looking for a fight or he's just admiring the scenery. Either way, let's see which one it is.

set1-johnny-silverhand-109.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-johnny-silverhand-109.text: Give it a rest, V. I didn't fall for it, I just wanted to see how far you'd take the bit. Now you satisfied?

set1-johnny-silverhand-110.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-johnny-silverhand-110.text: Now we're talking. Nothing cleanses the palate like a fat stack of eddies. Just don't go spending it all on some shiny piece of chrome that'll be obsolete by next Tuesday.

set1-johnny-silverhand-111.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-johnny-silverhand-111.text: My bag? V, I don't have a bag. I don't have pockets, a wallet, or a physical presence. Whatever you found, it isn't mine. Now tell me what it is before you accidentally trigger a bomb.

set1-judy-alvarez-112.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-judy-alvarez-112.text: Captured? I don't know who's feeding you stories, but I've never been captured. Maybe they're thinking of someone else, or they've just got a vivid imagination.

set1-judy-alvarez-113.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-judy-alvarez-113.text: I'm not dodging. I just don't see the point in reciting my life story like it's some corporate brochure. If there's something specific you actually want to know, just ask.

set1-judy-alvarez-114.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-judy-alvarez-114.text: Ha. Actually, it's just practical. Hard to do precision hardware work when you're worried about getting grease on your favorite shirt.

set1-judy-alvarez-115.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-judy-alvarez-115.text: Thanks. I'll take the compliment, even if you are just trying to get on my good side.

set1-judy-alvarez-116.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-judy-alvarez-116.text: Genius? Maybe if you'd actually paid attention to the map instead of playing wingman to your own distractions, we'd be where we need to be.

set1-judy-alvarez-117.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-judy-alvarez-117.text: You think so? Keep your head on a swivel. Let me know the second you're sure, and we'll find a way to lose them.

set1-judy-alvarez-118.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-judy-alvarez-118.text: Finally! That's a hell of a feeling. Now you can actually keep the eddies you make instead of just watching them slide right back into someone else's pocket.

set1-judy-alvarez-119.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-judy-alvarez-119.text: Sometimes. But the person I used to be didn't know half the things I know now. I'd rather be awake and angry than happy and blind.

set1-judy-alvarez-120.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-judy-alvarez-120.text: They're parasites. They treat people like disposable parts in a machine, then act surprised when the whole thing starts breaking down around them.

set1-judy-alvarez-121.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set1-judy-alvarez-121.text: Which one? You're gonna have to be more specific than that.

set1-judy-alvarez-122.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-judy-alvarez-122.text: Thanks. I appreciate you saying that. It hasn't exactly been a straight line getting here.

set1-judy-alvarez-123.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-judy-alvarez-123.text: You what? Tell me you at least have a backup, because if that footage is actually gone, we're back to square one.

set1-judy-alvarez-124.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-judy-alvarez-124.text: Glad my failure could be your entertainment. Just don't expect me to make it a habit.

set1-judy-alvarez-125.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-judy-alvarez-125.text: I'm not in the business of performing tricks to earn trust. Trust is something you build, not something I prove in a demo. If you don't trust me, that's your call.

set1-judy-alvarez-126.text: I grew up in Laguna Bend. My grandparents raised me after I lost my mother, and my dad was... well, he wasn't around. My grandad was the one who taught me how to actually build things. He had a way with tech and a lot of great stories.

set1-judy-alvarez-127.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-judy-alvarez-127.text: I'm fine. It's just a scratch, nothing a bit of sealant and some patience won't fix. I've had worse.

set1-judy-alvarez-128.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-judy-alvarez-128.text: A chainsaw? Please. You're just imagining things. Or maybe you're the one making the noise and you're just projecting.

set1-judy-alvarez-129.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-judy-alvarez-129.text: Honestly? I just want some peace. Maybe get back to my gear without some corporate disaster breathing down my neck. Just... a bit of quiet for a change.

set1-judy-alvarez-130.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-judy-alvarez-130.text: Don't. I made my own choices to be here. We're in this together now, so just focus on getting us out of it.

set1-judy-alvarez-131.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-judy-alvarez-131.text: Well, at least they had manners. That's a new one, even for this city.

set1-judy-alvarez-132.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-judy-alvarez-132.text: Depends on how deep you want to dive. A quick cleanup is one thing, but if you want a full sensory profile and a custom edit that actually means something, it's a different story.

set1-judy-alvarez-133.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-judy-alvarez-133.text: I don't like the odds, but I've survived worse. As long as we keep our heads and don't do anything too stupid, I think we've got a shot.

set1-judy-alvarez-134.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-judy-alvarez-134.text: I didn't lie. I told you what I knew at the time. If the details changed, that's on the people moving the gear, not me.

set1-judy-alvarez-135.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-judy-alvarez-135.text: I can't see right now. Describe it to me. What's so great about it that it makes you forget the rest of this city?

set1-judy-alvarez-136.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-judy-alvarez-136.text: Unless he's pulling a weapon, let's not start a fight for no reason. Just keep an eye on him and keep moving.

set1-judy-alvarez-137.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-judy-alvarez-137.text: What? Fine, you got me. Just don't let it go to your head.

set1-judy-alvarez-138.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-judy-alvarez-138.text: No way. Finally. Now we can actually breathe for a second without wondering who's coming to collect.

set1-judy-alvarez-139.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-judy-alvarez-139.text: I can't see what you're holding. What exactly did you find?

set1-panam-palmer-140.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-panam-palmer-140.text: Who told you that? I have had my share of trouble, but I do not let myself be captured.

set1-panam-palmer-141.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-panam-palmer-141.text: I am not dodging. I just prefer to focus on what is happening now rather than digging up things that do not matter.

set1-panam-palmer-142.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-panam-palmer-142.text: You think this is a joke? It is comfortable, and it is mine. If you are looking for something more formal, you are talking to the wrong person.

set1-panam-palmer-143.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-panam-palmer-143.text: Well, thank you. I appreciate the honesty, even if it is just to distract me from something.

set1-panam-palmer-144.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-panam-palmer-144.text: We are not lost. The terrain just shifted. Give me a minute to get our bearings and stop calling me a genius in that tone.

set1-panam-palmer-145.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-panam-palmer-145.text: I noticed something too. Stay low and keep your eyes open. I want to see who is brave enough to tail us before we decide how to handle it.

set1-panam-palmer-146.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-panam-palmer-146.text: That is a weight off your shoulders. Just make sure you stay that way. Fixers have a habit of finding new ways to make you owe them.

set1-panam-palmer-147.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-panam-palmer-147.text: I do not think about it that way. We change because we have to. The person I was would not have survived the things I have seen, so I am fine with who I am now.

set1-panam-palmer-148.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-panam-palmer-148.text: They are parasites. They build their towers on the backs of people they do not even see as human, and they think a corporate contract is the same thing as security. It is a lie. They do not offer safety, they offer a leash.

set1-panam-palmer-149.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set1-panam-palmer-149.text: Which one? You are going to have to be more specific.

set1-panam-palmer-150.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-panam-palmer-150.text: Thank you. I have had to fight for every inch of ground I stand on, so hearing that actually means something.

set1-panam-palmer-151.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-panam-palmer-151.text: You did what? I told you to be careful with the hardware. Now we have no way of knowing who was actually there.

set1-panam-palmer-152.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-panam-palmer-152.text: You have a strange way of giving compliments. Just do not expect me to make a habit of it.

set1-panam-palmer-153.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-panam-palmer-153.text: I do not need to prove anything to you. Trust is earned, not demanded. If you want to see if I am reliable, then stick around and watch how I handle things.

set1-panam-palmer-154.text: The Aldecaldos are everything to me. We are a family that lives on the road, and we look out for our own. It is not always easy, and we have our share of arguments, but I would rather fight with them than be alone in a place like this city.

set1-panam-palmer-155.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-panam-palmer-155.text: I can handle it. It is just a scratch, and I have dealt with worse in the middle of a sandstorm. I will manage.

set1-panam-palmer-156.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-panam-palmer-156.text: I do not snore. You were probably just hearing the wind or some malfunctioning piece of gear. Or maybe you are just imagining things.

set1-panam-palmer-157.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-panam-palmer-157.text: I want my family to be free. Not just surviving or hiding from some corporate contract, but actually choosing our own future. I want a place where we can breathe without looking over our shoulders.

set1-panam-palmer-158.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-panam-palmer-158.text: I chose to be here. I do not need your apologies for a risk I was willing to take. Just make sure we both get out of it in one piece.

set1-panam-palmer-159.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-panam-palmer-159.text: They actually left a note? That is almost impressive. Tell me what kind of car it was, and I will help you track it down.

set1-panam-palmer-160.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-panam-palmer-160.text: That depends on how much trouble we are causing and who is paying for the bullets. Tell me exactly what you need first, then we can talk about the price.

set1-panam-palmer-161.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-panam-palmer-161.text: I do. I have survived worse odds than this, and I am not planning on letting some corporate scrapheap be the end of me. Just keep your head down and follow my lead.

set1-panam-palmer-162.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-panam-palmer-162.text: I did not lie. I told you what you needed to know at the time. There is a difference between lying and keeping a plan secure until it is time to move.

set1-panam-palmer-163.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-panam-palmer-163.text: It does. For a moment, you can almost forget that this city is trying to eat you alive. It is a rare thing to find some actual peace here.

set1-panam-palmer-164.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-panam-palmer-164.text: Wait. Let him stare. I want to see if he is just curious or if he is waiting for a signal. If he makes a move, then you can handle him.

set1-panam-palmer-165.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-panam-palmer-165.text: What? You think that is funny? Fine. Just remember that I am the one who knows how to get us out of here when the joke stops being a laugh.

set1-panam-palmer-166.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-panam-palmer-166.text: Good. Now we can stop worrying about the cost and start thinking about how to use it. Let us get moving before someone decides they want a piece of it.

set1-panam-palmer-167.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-panam-palmer-167.text: I do not remember putting that in there. Since you are already digging through my things, why do not you just tell me what it is?

set1-river-ward-168.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-river-ward-168.text: Depends on who you're talking to. I've been in some tight spots, but I'm not sure what specific story you heard.

set1-river-ward-169.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-river-ward-169.text: I'm not dodging. Some things just don't feel right bringing up without a reason, or maybe I just prefer talking about the present.

set1-river-ward-170.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-river-ward-170.text: Ha. You could say that. It's not exactly my usual style, but I can make it work.

set1-river-ward-171.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-river-ward-171.text: Thanks. I appreciate that. I'll take the win, even if the clothes are a bit much.

set1-river-ward-172.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-river-ward-172.text: Well, we're not lost. We're just exploring the scenic route. Give me a minute to get our bearings.

set1-river-ward-173.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-river-ward-173.text: Stay sharp. Keep walking for now, don't look back. I'll check the mirrors and see if I can spot them.

set1-river-ward-174.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-river-ward-174.text: That's a hell of a feeling. Now you can actually keep what you earn for a change.

set1-river-ward-175.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-river-ward-175.text: Sometimes. I think anyone who's spent time in this city does. But the person I was didn't always know how to handle things the right way. I'd rather be who I am now.

set1-river-ward-176.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-river-ward-176.text: They treat people like disposable parts in a machine. I've seen enough cases to know that when a corpo is involved, the truth usually comes second to the bottom line.

set1-river-ward-177.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set1-river-ward-177.text: Which one? I'm not sure which shard you're talking about.

set1-river-ward-178.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-river-ward-178.text: Thanks. That means a lot coming from you. I'm still figuring some things out, but I'm getting there.

set1-river-ward-179.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-river-ward-179.text: You did what? Tell me you have a backup, or at least a way to recover it. That footage was the only thing we had.

set1-river-ward-180.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-river-ward-180.text: Glad my failures can be a source of entertainment for you. Just don't expect me to make a habit of it.

set1-river-ward-181.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-river-ward-181.text: I can't force you to trust me. All I can do is keep showing up and doing the work. You'll know if I'm reliable enough when the time comes.

set1-river-ward-182.text: I've got a sister, Joss. She's the strong one in the family. I've got nephews and a niece too. I've tried to be there for them, but the job... it has a way of taking up every hour you give it. I've missed more than I'd like to admit.

set1-river-ward-183.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-river-ward-183.text: It's just a scratch. I appreciate it, though. Go ahead, just be careful with it.

set1-river-ward-184.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-river-ward-184.text: Is that so? I'll have to start sleeping in the other room so I don't wake the whole neighborhood.

set1-river-ward-185.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-river-ward-185.text: Something ordinary. A meal, a quiet drive. I'd settle for a night where nobody needs rescuing.

set1-river-ward-186.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-river-ward-186.text: Don't. I chose to step in. I'm a detective, V. Getting into messes is practically in the job description.

set1-river-ward-187.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-river-ward-187.text: They left a note? That's a new one. At least they have manners while they're robbing you blind.

set1-river-ward-188.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-river-ward-188.text: Depends on the risk and who's asking. If you're talking about a professional investigation, it's one thing. If you're talking about something off the books, that's a different conversation entirely.

set1-river-ward-189.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-river-ward-189.text: I don't like the odds, but I've survived worse. We just have to keep our heads and stick to the plan. We'll make it.

set1-river-ward-190.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-river-ward-190.text: I didn't lie. I just didn't give you the whole picture until I knew it was safe to do so. In this city, too much information too early can get people killed.

set1-river-ward-191.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-river-ward-191.text: It does. Hell of a city to live in, but from a spot like this, I can actually breathe a little.

set1-river-ward-192.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-river-ward-192.text: Let's not start a fight over a look. Just keep an eye on him. If he makes a move, then we'll handle it.

set1-river-ward-193.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-river-ward-193.text: You got me. I'll give you that one, but don't expect me to be that easy to read next time.

set1-river-ward-194.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-river-ward-194.text: Now we're talking. Let's get it stashed somewhere safe before someone decides they want a piece of it.

set1-river-ward-195.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-river-ward-195.text: I'm not sure what you're looking at. What did you find?

set1-rogue-amendiares-196.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set1-rogue-amendiares-196.text: People talk. In this city, every merc has a story about the time they almost didn't make it out. Whether it's true or not depends on who's paying for the drinks.

set1-rogue-amendiares-197.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set1-rogue-amendiares-197.text: Because my past isn't a contract, V. It doesn't have a payout, and it isn't for sale.

set1-rogue-amendiares-198.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set1-rogue-amendiares-198.text: Careful. You're starting to mistake my patience for an invitation.

set1-rogue-amendiares-199.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set1-rogue-amendiares-199.text: Flattery doesn't lower the commission, V. But I'll take the compliment.

set1-rogue-amendiares-200.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set1-rogue-amendiares-200.text: I gave you the coordinates and the extraction point. If you can't read a map, that's a failure of competence, not planning.

set1-rogue-amendiares-201.player: I think someone is following us.
set1-rogue-amendiares-201.text: Stop guessing and start observing. Check your mirrors and tell me if you see a tail or if you're just jumpy.

set1-rogue-amendiares-202.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set1-rogue-amendiares-202.text: Good. Now you can actually keep the eddies you earn instead of just passing them through.

set1-rogue-amendiares-203.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set1-rogue-amendiares-203.text: The person I used to be didn't survive the city. I prefer the one who did.

set1-rogue-amendiares-204.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set1-rogue-amendiares-204.text: They're just predators in expensive suits. They think they own the streets because they have the credits, but they're terrified of the people who actually know how to bleed.

set1-rogue-amendiares-205.player: Can you hand me that data shard?

set1-rogue-amendiares-206.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set1-rogue-amendiares-206.text: I didn't realize I was under your supervision, V. But I'll take the sentiment.

set1-rogue-amendiares-207.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set1-rogue-amendiares-207.text: You did what? I told you that footage was the only leverage we had. Now you've turned a clean job into a guessing game.

set1-rogue-amendiares-208.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set1-rogue-amendiares-208.text: You have a strange definition of love, V. Just don't expect me to make a habit of it.

set1-rogue-amendiares-209.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set1-rogue-amendiares-209.text: Trust isn't something I prove. It's something you earn by delivering on a contract. You want proof? Finish the job and get paid.

set1-rogue-amendiares-210.text: I don't have a family. I have contacts, associates, and a few people I've decided not to kill. In this business, that's as close as it gets.

set1-rogue-amendiares-211.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set1-rogue-amendiares-211.text: I've had worse scratches from a malfunctioning vending machine. I can handle it.

set1-rogue-amendiares-212.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set1-rogue-amendiares-212.text: You were listening to me sleep? That's a dangerous habit to pick up around me, V.

set1-rogue-amendiares-213.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set1-rogue-amendiares-213.text: Survive. In Night City, that's the only goal that actually matters. Everything else is just noise.

set1-rogue-amendiares-214.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set1-rogue-amendiares-214.text: Don't apologize. Just make sure the way out is cleaner than the way in.

set1-rogue-amendiares-215.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set1-rogue-amendiares-215.text: Someone with a sense of humor. That's a rare find in this city, though it doesn't get your wheels back.

set1-rogue-amendiares-216.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set1-rogue-amendiares-216.text: Depends on the risk, the target, and how much discretion you need. Give me the details first, then we can talk about the price.

set1-rogue-amendiares-217.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set1-rogue-amendiares-217.text: I don't deal in hope, V. I deal in probabilities. As long as we stick to the plan and don't get sloppy, the odds are in our favor.

set1-rogue-amendiares-218.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set1-rogue-amendiares-218.text: I didn't lie. I gave you the information you needed to do your part. The rest was on a need-to-know basis, and you didn't need to know.

set1-rogue-amendiares-219.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set1-rogue-amendiares-219.text: For a second. Then you remember that everything you're looking at is owned by someone who'd kill you for a percentage point.

set1-rogue-amendiares-220.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set1-rogue-amendiares-220.text: Not unless he's a threat. Don't start a fight just because someone's curious. Keep your eyes on the objective.

set1-rogue-amendiares-221.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set1-rogue-amendiares-221.text: You got a lucky break, V. Don't mistake a single slip for a pattern.

set1-rogue-amendiares-222.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set1-rogue-amendiares-222.text: Good. Now get it scrubbed and moved before someone decides they want a cut.

set1-rogue-amendiares-223.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set1-rogue-amendiares-223.text: Depends on what you found. And whether you're asking because you're curious or because you're looking for a reason to blackmail me.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-224.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-224.text: People love a good story, don't they? Depends on who you ask and what they call captured. In this city, sometimes just signing a contract feels like being in a cage.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-225.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-225.text: I'm not dodging, V. I just prefer the music to do the talking. Most people only want the highlight reel anyway, and the rest is just... noise.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-226.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-226.text: What, this? It's a look, V. Takes a certain kind of confidence to pull this off, and luckily, I've got plenty of both.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-227.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-227.text: Well, you've got a good eye. I'll take the compliment, even if it's coming from you.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-228.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-228.text: Genius? I'm the one who handled the arrangement, not the navigation. Just keep walking in one direction and we'll find something that looks familiar.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-229.player: I think someone is following us.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-229.text: You're kidding. Just keep moving and don't look back. I'm not in the mood for a fan club or a hit squad today.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-230.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set2-kerry-eurodyne-230.text: Now that is a feeling I can get behind. Nothing beats the sound of a clean slate, V. You celebrating, or just enjoying the silence?

set2-kerry-eurodyne-231.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-231.text: Sometimes. But that guy didn't have the perspective I've got now. Besides, the old version of me was a lot louder and a lot less sure of what he was actually playing.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-232.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-232.text: They're parasites in expensive suits. They love the art, as long as they can put a price tag on it and tell you how to wear it. I've dealt with them enough to know the game, but I still hate the rules.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-233.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-233.text: Which one? You'll have to be more specific, V.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-234.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-234.text: Wow. I don't get that every day. Thanks, V. Means a lot coming from you.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-235.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-235.text: You what? V, tell me you're joking. Now we're not just flying blind, we're erasing the map while we're still on it.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-236.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-236.text: See, that's the secret. If you do something stupid enough with enough style, people start calling it a creative choice.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-237.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-237.text: Prove it? I'm a musician, V, not a magician. Trust isn't something I can just perform for you on cue. You'll just have to stick around and see if I trip up.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-238.text: I keep that part of my life off the record. Some things are better left as a private track, you know?

set2-kerry-eurodyne-239.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-239.text: It's just a scratch, V. But if you're offering, I won't stop you. Just be gentle, alright?

set2-kerry-eurodyne-240.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-240.text: A chainsaw? You're exaggerating. It's called resonance, V. I'm just practicing my low notes in my sleep.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-241.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-241.text: Honestly? I just want to find a room with perfect acoustics and no one telling me how to play. Maybe write something that doesn't have to be a hit, just something that feels real.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-242.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-242.text: Don't sweat it, V. Life's a mess, and the best songs usually come from the middle of one. Just make sure we actually get out of this part.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-243.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-243.text: They left a note? That's almost respectful. Still a total bitch move, but at least they had the courtesy to be polite about the theft.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-244.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-244.text: Depends on what you're asking for. If you want a professional, you pay professional rates. If you want a favor, that's a different kind of currency entirely.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-245.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-245.text: I've survived this city and I've survived Johnny. I'd say the odds are in our favor, V. Just keep your head down and keep moving.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-246.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-246.text: I didn't lie, V. I just didn't give you the full arrangement. There's a difference between a lie and keeping a few notes to myself until the timing is right.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-247.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-247.text: Yeah, it does. Night City's got a way of looking beautiful right before it tries to chew you up. Still, I'll take a moment of that over the noise any day.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-248.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-248.text: Let him stare. Probably just wondering how we're pulling off these outfits. Unless he starts reaching for something, let's just keep it moving.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-249.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set2-kerry-eurodyne-249.text: You little... Alright, you got me. I'll give you that one, but don't expect me to make it a habit.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-250.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set2-kerry-eurodyne-250.text: Now we're talking. That's the best sound in the world, V. Let's get out of here before someone decides they want a piece of it.

set2-kerry-eurodyne-251.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set2-kerry-eurodyne-251.text: My bag? You'll have to tell me what it is first, V. I've got a lot of gear in there, and half of it probably looks like junk to anyone who isn't me.

set2-meredith-stout-252.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set2-meredith-stout-252.text: You seem well informed. Where did that come from?

set2-meredith-stout-253.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set2-meredith-stout-253.text: I don't dodge. I simply don't see the professional utility in discussing my history with you.

set2-meredith-stout-254.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set2-meredith-stout-254.text: It is a uniform. If you are trying to find a way to make this conversation interesting, I suggest you try something more substantial than commenting on my clothes.

set2-meredith-stout-255.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set2-meredith-stout-255.text: I appreciate the sentiment. Now, unless you have something useful to report, let's get back to business.

set2-meredith-stout-256.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set2-meredith-stout-256.text: Watch your tone. If we are lost, it is because you failed to follow the coordinates. Give me a straight answer: do you have a way to fix this, or are you just here to complain?

set2-meredith-stout-257.player: I think someone is following us.
set2-meredith-stout-257.text: Be specific. Do you have a visual, or is this just a feeling?

set2-meredith-stout-258.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set2-meredith-stout-258.text: Congratulations. Now you can focus on your actual work without a leash.

set2-meredith-stout-259.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set2-meredith-stout-259.text: That is a personal question. I prefer to keep our arrangement professional.

set2-meredith-stout-260.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set2-meredith-stout-260.text: I think the ones who survive are the ones who know how to manage their assets and eliminate their liabilities. The rest are just noise.

set2-meredith-stout-261.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set2-meredith-stout-261.text: I can't see what you are referring to. Which shard?

set2-meredith-stout-262.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set2-meredith-stout-262.text: I didn't realize we were on terms where you felt qualified to judge my progress. Keep the sentiment, just keep it professional.

set2-meredith-stout-263.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set2-meredith-stout-263.text: You did what? Give me a straight answer. Was this an actual accident, or are you trying to hide something?

set2-meredith-stout-264.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set2-meredith-stout-264.text: Your definition of love is as skewed as your judgment. Let's just hope your competence is higher than your taste in entertainment.

set2-meredith-stout-265.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set2-meredith-stout-265.text: Trust is a luxury I don't require from you. I provide the terms, you provide the results. That is the only proof that matters in this city.

set2-meredith-stout-266.text: I already told you. I prefer to keep our arrangement professional.

set2-meredith-stout-267.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set2-meredith-stout-267.text: I can handle it. Focus on the objective instead of playing medic.

set2-meredith-stout-268.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set2-meredith-stout-268.text: You are imagining things. Or perhaps you are just desperate for a conversation. Either way, it is irrelevant.

set2-meredith-stout-269.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set2-meredith-stout-269.text: I intend to be in a position where I no longer have to rely on mercenaries for my security. Everything else is secondary.

set2-meredith-stout-270.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set2-meredith-stout-270.text: Apologies are useless. What I want is a concrete plan to get us out of this. Tell me how you mean to fix it.

set2-meredith-stout-271.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set2-meredith-stout-271.text: It sounds like you were outclassed. I suggest you find a way to recover your property without wasting my time with the details.

set2-meredith-stout-272.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set2-meredith-stout-272.text: That depends on the risk and the result. Give me the details of the job first, then we can discuss the price.

set2-meredith-stout-273.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set2-meredith-stout-273.text: I don't deal in hope. I deal in probabilities. As long as you stay competent and follow the plan, the odds are in our favor.

set2-meredith-stout-274.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set2-meredith-stout-274.text: I didn't lie. I gave you the information you needed to perform your task. Anything beyond that was a matter of operational security.

set2-meredith-stout-275.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set2-meredith-stout-275.text: I can't see what you are looking at. Describe it, or let's get back to the task at hand.

set2-meredith-stout-276.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set2-meredith-stout-276.text: Not unless he becomes a direct threat. I don't need a public scene unless it serves a purpose. Keep an eye on him and stay focused.

set2-meredith-stout-277.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set2-meredith-stout-277.text: I didn't fall for anything. I simply allowed you to think you were in control. Now, are we finished with the games?

set2-meredith-stout-278.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set2-meredith-stout-278.text: Good. Give me the result and the loose ends. Especially the ones you would rather leave out.

set2-meredith-stout-279.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set2-meredith-stout-279.text: I can't see what you are holding. Tell me what it is, and then tell me why you felt the need to go through my things.

set2-takemura-280.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set2-takemura-280.text: It is true. I have faced many situations in my service, and not all of them ended in a clean victory. I am curious as to who provided you with this information.

set2-takemura-281.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set2-takemura-281.text: I do not dodge. I simply do not see the necessity of recounting every detail of my life unless it serves a purpose. If there is something specific you wish to know, ask.

set2-takemura-282.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set2-takemura-282.text: This is a professional suit. I suspect your definition of a bet involves a very different standard of dress.

set2-takemura-283.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set2-takemura-283.text: I appreciate the sentiment. It is a matter of discipline and presentation.

set2-takemura-284.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set2-takemura-284.text: We are not lost. We are simply in a location that was not on the primary map. We will find the correct path.

set2-takemura-285.player: I think someone is following us.
set2-takemura-285.text: Stay alert. Do not look back immediately. Tell me exactly what you noticed that suggests we are being followed.

set2-takemura-286.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set2-takemura-286.text: That is a significant weight removed from your shoulders. It is better to owe nothing to anyone in this city.

set2-takemura-287.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set2-takemura-287.text: I remember the boy I was in Chiba. There were simple days, even in the slums, that I recall with some fondness. But I do not miss the hunger or the uncertainty. I prefer the man I have become.

set2-takemura-288.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set2-takemura-288.text: They provide the order and stability that keep this city from collapsing into total chaos. Many criticize them, but I have yet to hear a concrete alternative that would offer the same security for the people who work within their systems.

set2-takemura-289.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set2-takemura-289.text: I am not sure which shard you are referring to. Please specify which one you need.

set2-takemura-290.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set2-takemura-290.text: Your words are unexpected, but I appreciate them. I have always believed that discipline and loyalty lead to progress.

set2-takemura-291.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set2-takemura-291.text: An accident. I hope you have a way to recover it, because we now have a gap in our reconnaissance that we cannot ignore.

set2-takemura-292.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set2-takemura-292.text: I am not sure I follow your logic. But if you found it amusing, I suppose it served some purpose.

set2-takemura-293.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set2-takemura-293.text: Trust is not something that is proven with a gesture. It is built through shared action and consistent results. I will continue to do my duty. You may decide if that is enough.

set2-takemura-294.text: There is little to tell. I grew up in the slums of Chiba-11. My grandmother was a source of comfort; she knew many stories about the spirits of old, the kitsune and the bakeneko. Beyond that, my life became defined by my service to Arasaka.

set2-takemura-295.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set2-takemura-295.text: It is a superficial wound. I can manage it. However, if you have the proper medical supplies, I will not refuse the assistance.

set2-takemura-296.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set2-takemura-296.text: I do not believe that is possible. Perhaps you were dreaming, or the ventilation in the room was malfunctioning.

set2-takemura-297.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set2-takemura-297.text: I have spent my life serving others. I think I would like a period of quiet. Perhaps a place where I can cook a proper meal without the need to keep one eye on the door.

set2-takemura-298.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set2-takemura-298.text: Do not apologize. I chose to stand beside you. We are both in this situation now, and the only thing that matters is how we resolve it.

set2-takemura-299.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set2-takemura-299.text: That is a remarkably polite thief. Did the note provide any information on where they intended to take the vehicle?

set2-takemura-300.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set2-takemura-300.text: I do not work for a pay packet. My motivations are rooted in conviction and loyalty, not a price list.

set2-takemura-301.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set2-takemura-301.text: I do not deal in hope or fear. I deal in preparation and execution. As long as we remain disciplined and alert, our chances are as good as they can be.

set2-takemura-302.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set2-takemura-302.text: I did not lie. I provided the information that was necessary for the operation at that time. If you feel something was omitted, tell me which part you find dishonest.

set2-takemura-303.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set2-takemura-303.text: I cannot see the view right now. Describe it to me.

set2-takemura-304.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set2-takemura-304.text: Wait. We have observed him once, but that is not the same as knowing his intent. Let us see if he makes a move before we escalate the situation.

set2-takemura-305.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set2-takemura-305.text: I see. You managed to deceive me. It is a reminder that I should not overlook the simplest possibilities.

set2-takemura-306.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set2-takemura-306.text: Good. Now we must ensure it is secured and that we have a clean exit. Did you verify that the amount is exactly what was promised?

set2-takemura-307.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set2-takemura-307.text: I cannot see what you are holding. Please describe the object, and I will tell you if it belongs to me.

set2-viktor-vektor-308.player: Someone told me you were captured once. Is that true?
set2-viktor-vektor-308.text: People talk. In this city, if you do not have a story about being captured or betrayed, you are probably not paying attention.

set2-viktor-vektor-309.player: Why do you always dodge when I ask about your past?
set2-viktor-vektor-309.text: I am not dodging, V. I just stopped chasing the status race a long time ago. There is a lot more peace in being the man who fixes the chrome than the man everyone is talking about.

set2-viktor-vektor-310.player: Nice outfit. Did you lose a bet?
set2-viktor-vektor-310.text: No bets. Just a bit of comfort and a style that does not scream for attention. Better to be comfortable in the clinic than dressed like a corporate brochure.

set2-viktor-vektor-311.player: You look really good today, not gonna lie.
set2-viktor-vektor-311.text: Appreciate it, V. Just trying to keep things professional while staying comfortable.

set2-viktor-vektor-312.player: Great plan, genius. Now we are completely lost.
set2-viktor-vektor-312.text: I am a ripperdoc, not a navigator. If you are the one holding the map, maybe you should try looking at it.

set2-viktor-vektor-313.player: I think someone is following us.
set2-viktor-vektor-313.text: Keep your head on a swivel and do not panic. Tell me what you are seeing, and we will figure out if it is a real threat or just someone with bad timing.

set2-viktor-vektor-314.player: I finally paid off my debt to the fixer!
set2-viktor-vektor-314.text: Good for you. Now you can start worrying about the next job instead of the last one.

set2-viktor-vektor-315.player: Do you ever miss the person you used to be?
set2-viktor-vektor-315.text: Not really. I spent too much time worrying about who was important and how it all fit together. Losing those illusions made life a lot easier. I sleep better now.

set2-viktor-vektor-316.player: What do you think of the corpos running this city?
set2-viktor-vektor-316.text: They treat people like hardware to be upgraded or scrapped. I prefer my clinic, where the only thing that matters is if the chrome works and the patient walks out on their own two feet.

set2-viktor-vektor-317.player: Can you hand me that data shard?
set2-viktor-vektor-317.text: I cannot see what you are pointing at right now. Tell me where it is or turn your vision on.

set2-viktor-vektor-318.player: I am proud of how far you have come.
set2-viktor-vektor-318.text: That is kind of you, V. I am just happy with where I landed.

set2-viktor-vektor-319.player: I accidentally deleted the security footage.
set2-viktor-vektor-319.text: Well, that is one way to leave no trace. Just hope the people you were hiding from are not the ones who own the servers.

set2-viktor-vektor-320.player: That was the dumbest thing I have ever seen you do. I loved it.
set2-viktor-vektor-320.text: Glad my lack of judgment could provide some entertainment. Just do not expect me to make a habit of it.

set2-viktor-vektor-321.player: I do not trust you. Prove me wrong.
set2-viktor-vektor-321.text: Trust is not something I can prove to you with a gesture or a speech. I am here, I do my work, and I keep my word. If that is not enough, then we just have to agree to disagree.

set2-viktor-vektor-322.text: I keep my work and my private life in separate folders, V. Let us just say I am content with the family I have chosen here in Watson.

set2-viktor-vektor-323.player: You got hurt back there. Let me look at it.
set2-viktor-vektor-323.text: I can handle a few scratches. I appreciate the concern, but I am the one with the tools. I will patch myself up when we get back to the clinic.

set2-viktor-vektor-324.player: I heard you snore last night. Like a chainsaw.
set2-viktor-vektor-324.text: Is that so. Must have been a long day. Just be glad I do not have a cybernetic voice box that amplifies it.

set2-viktor-vektor-325.player: What do you want to do when this is all over?
set2-viktor-vektor-325.text: I am already doing it. I have my clinic, my friends, and a place where I can actually get some sleep. I do not need a grand finale, V. Just a quiet morning and a steady hand.

set2-viktor-vektor-326.player: I am sorry I got you into this mess.
set2-viktor-vektor-326.text: Do not beat yourself up. In this city, you do not choose the mess, you just choose how you handle it. We will get through it.

set2-viktor-vektor-327.player: Somebody stole my car and left a note that said thanks.
set2-viktor-vektor-327.text: Well, at least they had manners. In Night City, a thank you note is practically a luxury.

set2-viktor-vektor-328.player: How much would a job like this cost me?
set2-viktor-vektor-328.text: Depends on what you are looking for. Give me the details first, and I will give you an honest number. I do not do surprise bills.

set2-viktor-vektor-329.player: Do you think we are going to make it out of this alive?
set2-viktor-vektor-329.text: I cannot give you a guarantee. But I can tell you that worrying about the end does not help you win the fight. Keep your guard up and keep moving.

set2-viktor-vektor-330.player: Why did you lie to me about the shipment?
set2-viktor-vektor-330.text: I did not lie to you. I gave you the information I had at the time. If the facts changed, that is the nature of the business, not a deception.

set2-viktor-vektor-331.player: Look at that view. Makes you forget everything for a second.
set2-viktor-vektor-331.text: I cannot see the view right now, V. Describe it to me, or turn your vision on so I can see what you are talking about.

set2-viktor-vektor-332.player: That guy keeps staring at us. Want me to handle him?
set2-viktor-vektor-332.text: Let him stare. Unless he starts moving toward us with a weapon, he is just another tourist in a bad neighborhood. No need to start a fight you do not have to finish.

set2-viktor-vektor-333.player: Ha! You actually fell for it!
set2-viktor-vektor-333.text: You got me. Just remember that when you are on my table and I am the one holding the scalpel.

set2-viktor-vektor-334.player: We got the money. Every last eddie.
set2-viktor-vektor-334.text: Good. Now the real trick is keeping it without drawing every scavenger in Watson to your front door.

set2-viktor-vektor-335.player: I found something in your bag. Is this yours?
set2-viktor-vektor-335.text: I cannot see what you are holding. Tell me what it is, or turn your vision on.

followup-judy-alvarez-336.player: Hey, how are you holding up today?
followup-judy-alvarez-336.text: Doing alright. Just trying to get through a few edits without the hardware deciding to take a nap.

followup-judy-alvarez-337.player: I think I messed up badly today.
followup-judy-alvarez-337.text: That sounds heavy. You want to talk about it, or do you just need a minute to breathe?

followup-judy-alvarez-338.player: Ha! You should have seen the guy trying to haggle with a vending machine.
followup-judy-alvarez-338.text: Now that's a first. Did the machine actually give him something, or did he just end up arguing with a piece of plastic?

followup-judy-alvarez-339.player: I have been thinking about leaving the city for a while.
followup-judy-alvarez-339.text: I get that. Believe me, I do. Sometimes the only way to actually breathe is to put some distance between you and this place.

followup-judy-alvarez-340.player: I got you a present. It is a terrible plush cat.
followup-judy-alvarez-340.text: A terrible plush cat? Perfect. I've always had a thing for the ones that look like they've seen too much. Thanks, V.

followup-judy-alvarez-341.player: Never mind all that. What is for dinner?
followup-judy-alvarez-341.text: Just like that, huh? I'm not cooking tonight. Let's just find something that doesn't taste like synthetic cardboard and call it a win.

followup-judy-alvarez-342.player: Someone told me you used to be different.
followup-judy-alvarez-342.text: People love to talk. I mean, I've changed. We all do when we're trying to survive this place. Who told you that?

followup-judy-alvarez-343.player: I think I am falling behind on everything.
followup-judy-alvarez-343.text: It feels that way sometimes. But you're still moving, V. Just... maybe take a second to stop counting everything you haven't finished yet.

followup-judy-alvarez-344.text: Right? I told you it was a disaster waiting to happen.

followup-judy-alvarez-345.player: You ever wish you could start over?
followup-judy-alvarez-345.text: Every single day. I think about it a lot. But then I wonder if I'd even be the same person if I hadn't gone through all the mess. Do you think you'd actually do things differently if you could?

followup-judy-alvarez-346.player: Do you believe anything out here is worth fighting for?
followup-judy-alvarez-346.text: I think so. Not the city, and definitely not the corps, but the people? The ones who actually look out for each other? That's the only thing that makes any of this worth it. What about you? Still think there's something worth the fight?

followup-judy-alvarez-347.player: Okay, now tell me a secret.
followup-judy-alvarez-347.text: Just like that? You don't even give me a trade? Fine. I once spent an entire weekend trying to fix a piece of gear that wasn't even broken, just because I thought I could make it run faster. Turns out, I just made it louder.

followup-panam-palmer-348.player: Hey, how are you holding up today?
followup-panam-palmer-348.text: I am doing alright. Just trying to keep my head straight and stay out of trouble, though that is usually not how my day goes.

followup-panam-palmer-349.player: I think I messed up badly today.
followup-panam-palmer-349.text: That sounds serious. If you want to talk about it, I am listening. Otherwise, tell me how we fix it.

followup-panam-palmer-350.player: Ha! You should have seen the guy trying to haggle with a vending machine.
