followup-panam-palmer-350.text: Now that is a new one. I wonder if the machine actually gave him a discount, or if he just ended up arguing with a piece of plastic.

followup-panam-palmer-351.player: I have been thinking about leaving the city for a while.
followup-panam-palmer-351.text: I can understand that. There is a whole world outside those walls where you can actually see the horizon without a skyscraper in the way. It is a different kind of hard, but it is a lot more honest.

followup-panam-palmer-352.player: I got you a present. It is a terrible plush cat.
followup-panam-palmer-352.text: A plush cat? I did not see that coming. It is hideous. I love it.

followup-panam-palmer-353.player: Never mind all that. What is for dinner?
followup-panam-palmer-353.text: Just like that, we move on. I am not picky, as long as it is not some synthetic sludge from a vending machine. What are you craving?

followup-panam-palmer-354.player: Someone told me you used to be different.
followup-panam-palmer-354.text: People love to talk, do they not? I have changed, sure. Life on the road and the things I have had to deal with tend to do that to a person. I am who I need to be to protect my own.

followup-panam-palmer-355.player: I think I am falling behind on everything.
followup-panam-palmer-355.text: Stop. You are doing the best you can in a city that wants to chew you up. Just take it one step at a time... you do not have to carry everything at once.

followup-panam-palmer-356.text: Right? I could not believe the look on their face. It is not every day you see someone that confident be that wrong.

followup-panam-palmer-357.player: You ever wish you could start over?
followup-panam-palmer-357.text: Every now and then. But starting over usually means leaving something behind, and I am not sure I am ready to let go of everything that made me who I am. What about you? You thinking of a clean slate?

followup-panam-palmer-358.player: Do you believe anything out here is worth fighting for?
followup-panam-palmer-358.text: Not the city, no. But the people? The ones who actually give a damn about each other? That is the only thing that ever was worth fighting for. Everything else is just noise.

followup-panam-palmer-359.player: Okay, now tell me a secret.
followup-panam-palmer-359.text: Just like that, you want a secret? You are going to have to earn that, V. I do not just hand out my private business because you asked nicely.

set3-alex-000.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-alex-000.text: Scared is a strong word. I prefer to call it a heightened state of professional awareness. Though, I will admit, the timing was a bit too close for my liking.

set3-alex-001.text: I was making sure we weren't being followed. Besides, the world doesn't actually end if I'm five minutes behind schedule.

set3-alex-002.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-alex-002.text: I won't judge. As long as they are edible, I'm not complaining.

set3-alex-003.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-alex-003.text: That is a dangerous question to ask someone in my line of work. Let's just say the list is shorter than I would like it to be.

set3-alex-004.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-alex-004.text: It was a messy piece of work. But we're still standing, which is more than I can say for the other side.

set3-alex-005.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-alex-005.text: Now you have me curious. Fine, eyes closed. Just don't make me regret it.

set3-alex-006.text: Well, look at you. Does that come with a raise, or just more paperwork and a fancier title?

set3-alex-007.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-alex-007.text: Some things are better left as footnotes. Besides, the story is usually a lot more exciting when you don't know all the details.

set3-alex-008.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-alex-008.text: Maybe that is the point. In my experience, being remembered usually means you left a trail someone can follow.

set3-alex-009.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-alex-009.text: I have spent seven years pretending to be someone I'm not. Talking my way out of a jam is the only part of the job I actually enjoy.

set3-alex-010.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-alex-010.text: Every single day. But the alternative is usually a lot more expensive.

set3-alex-011.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-alex-011.text: It's fine. A bit stiff, but nothing a little chrome and patience can't fix. Thanks for noticing, though.

set3-alex-012.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-alex-012.text: Now that is a plan I can get behind. Just tell me where we're going, and I'll start packing.

set3-alex-013.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-alex-013.text: I know. It is part of the charm. Keeps people from taking me too seriously.

set3-alex-014.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-alex-014.text: A villa on the Riviera. Champagne, sweet fruit, and a place where the only role I have to play is myself.

set3-alex-015.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-alex-015.text: I see. I suppose that simplifies things, even if it is a hell of a way to go.

set3-alex-016.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-alex-016.text: I'm full of surprises. Besides, I wanted to see if you'd actually be here waiting for me.

set3-alex-017.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-alex-017.text: That sounds like the best idea I have heard all day. Lead the way.

set3-alex-018.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-alex-018.text: Only one? I must be losing my touch. I usually attract a few more than that.

set3-alex-019.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-alex-019.text: I've got it, really. But if you're insisting on playing tailor, I suppose I can manage to stay still for a minute.

set3-alex-020.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-alex-020.text: A very demanding teacher and a lot of hours in the field. Let's just say the training was thorough, even if the benefits package was lacking.

set3-alex-021.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-alex-021.text: Please tell me you didn't wrap it around a pole. How bad are we talking?

set3-alex-022.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-alex-022.text: We improvise. That is usually where I do my best work anyway.

set3-alex-023.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-alex-023.text: Because for a long time, I didn't have a choice. And habits are hard to break, even when you hate the routine.

set3-alex-024.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-alex-024.text: Lost in the market? I'll forgive you this time, but next time, try to remember which way is north.

set3-alex-025.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-alex-025.text: Did you now? I hope the redacted parts were the most interesting. Those are usually where the real stories are.

set3-alex-026.text: Now you are talking my language. I'll hold you to that.

set3-alex-027.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-alex-027.text: The city doesn't change. It just finds new ways to eat people. The only way to see something different is to actually leave.

set3-evelyn-parker-028.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-evelyn-parker-028.text: Fear is a luxury for people who have a safety net. I prefer to call it a heightened sense of awareness.

set3-evelyn-parker-029.text: I was ensuring we weren't being followed. I imagine you'd prefer a late start over a short one.

set3-evelyn-parker-030.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-evelyn-parker-030.text: I wouldn't dream of it. As long as they aren't from a vending machine, I'm sure they're a delicacy.

set3-evelyn-parker-031.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-evelyn-parker-031.text: Trust is a heavy word. I have people I rely on, and people I believe in, but I rarely give both to the same person.

set3-evelyn-parker-032.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-evelyn-parker-032.text: It was a messy piece of work. But it proves that whoever is watching us is getting desperate.

set3-evelyn-parker-033.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-evelyn-parker-033.text: You're making this a performance. Fine, they're closed.

set3-evelyn-parker-034.text: I hope that means you're finally getting paid what you're worth. Or does it just mean you have more people reporting to you?

set3-evelyn-parker-035.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-evelyn-parker-035.text: Some things are better left as a blur. Besides, I think you enjoy the mystery more than you would the actual story.

set3-evelyn-parker-036.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-evelyn-parker-036.text: Most people in this city are just ghosts before they even stop breathing. I think there is a certain freedom in being forgotten.

set3-evelyn-parker-037.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-evelyn-parker-037.text: I don't think I can. I know I can. It is usually a matter of finding the one thing the other person is actually afraid to lose.

set3-evelyn-parker-038.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-evelyn-parker-038.text: It is not about being strong. It is about knowing which mask to wear so no one sees how tired I actually am.

set3-evelyn-parker-039.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-evelyn-parker-039.text: It is a dull ache for now. I have dealt with worse, though I appreciate that you noticed.

set3-evelyn-parker-040.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-evelyn-parker-040.text: That is a bold thought. The question is whether you are running toward something, or just trying to outrun the city.

set3-evelyn-parker-041.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-evelyn-parker-041.text: I know. It is a useful way to see who is actually paying attention.

set3-evelyn-parker-042.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-evelyn-parker-042.text: I would buy a ticket to somewhere the air doesn't taste like metal. And then I would make sure I never had to ask anyone for permission again.

set3-evelyn-parker-043.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-evelyn-parker-043.text: I see. The city has a way of cleaning up loose ends far faster than anyone expects.

set3-evelyn-parker-044.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-evelyn-parker-044.text: You sound surprised. I told you I would be here, and I generally prefer to keep my word.

set3-evelyn-parker-045.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-evelyn-parker-045.text: That sounds like a necessary change of pace. Lead the way.

set3-evelyn-parker-046.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-evelyn-parker-046.text: Rumors are the only thing that travel faster than bullets in this city. The real question is who is paying, and why they think I am worth the effort.

set3-evelyn-parker-047.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-evelyn-parker-047.text: I am holding still. Just try not to make it look like a street doc patched it together.

set3-evelyn-parker-048.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-evelyn-parker-048.text: Necessity is a very effective teacher. In my line of work, knowing how to handle yourself is the only real security you have.

set3-evelyn-parker-049.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-evelyn-parker-049.text: I can tell by your tone. Please tell me it is something that can be fixed with a few eddies and a very talented mechanic.

set3-evelyn-parker-050.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-evelyn-parker-050.text: We don't plan for it to go sideways. We plan for how to survive when it does.

set3-evelyn-parker-051.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-evelyn-parker-051.text: Because the things I want are here. I can tolerate the city if it means I am one step closer to leaving it on my own terms.

set3-evelyn-parker-052.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-evelyn-parker-052.text: Lost in the market? I hope you at least found something interesting to justify the delay.

set3-evelyn-parker-053.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-evelyn-parker-053.text: Files are just a collection of things people wanted to remember. I would be curious to know which parts you found interesting, and which parts you think are true.

set3-evelyn-parker-054.text: I will hold you to that. I think we both earned a drink that we didn't have to negotiate for.

set3-evelyn-parker-055.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-evelyn-parker-055.text: The city doesn't change. It just finds new ways to sell the same old lies to people who still believe they can win.

set3-jackie-welles-056.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-jackie-welles-056.text: Scared? Please, V. I was just making sure the scenery was appreciating me. But yeah, for a second there, I thought we were gonna be nothing more than a couple of stains on the pavement.

set3-jackie-welles-057.text: Hey, give a guy a break, hermano! Had a little situation with the bike, and then I saw a noodle stand that looked too good to pass up. You can't start a big job on an empty stomach.

set3-jackie-welles-058.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-jackie-welles-058.text: Who's laughing? I'm just admiring the effort! Pass them over, V. I'm starving.

set3-jackie-welles-059.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-jackie-welles-059.text: That is a heavy question for a morning, V. My mama, for sure. Always has been. Beyond that, there are a few people who have had my back when things got ugly, but family is the only thing that is absolute.

set3-jackie-welles-060.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-jackie-welles-060.text: Tell me about it. For a heartbeat there, I really thought we were done. But hey, we're still breathing, right? That's the part that counts.

set3-jackie-welles-061.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-jackie-welles-061.text: Oh, for real? Alright, alright, eyes shut. I'm not peeking! Now don't make me wait, choom, the suspense is killing me.

set3-jackie-welles-062.text: No way! I knew you had it in you, V! Tell me everything. We gotta celebrate this, for real. I'm thinking a bottle of the good stuff and the biggest meal in Heywood.

set3-jackie-welles-063.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-jackie-welles-063.text: Some things are better left in the dust, V. Let's just say I learned a few lessons about who to trust and how to keep my head down. We'll get to it eventually, maybe over a drink.

set3-jackie-welles-064.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-jackie-welles-064.text: Now, why you gotta go and get all dark on me? Listen, that is why we push for the big leagues, V. We do something so loud, so spectacular, that this city has no choice but to remember our names. And even if the city forgets, we got each other. That is enough for me.

set3-jackie-welles-065.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-jackie-welles-065.text: Watch me, V. A little charm, a few well-placed lies, and a smile that says I'm not thinking about the gun in my pocket. It works more often than you'd think.

set3-jackie-welles-066.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-jackie-welles-066.text: Sometimes. It gets heavy, you know? Always gotta be the one with the plan or the one taking the hits so others don't have to. But then I look at you, or I think about my mama, and it feels worth it. Besides, someone's gotta keep us from falling apart.

set3-jackie-welles-067.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-jackie-welles-067.text: Stings like a bitch, I'll give you that. But it's nothing a little time with Viktor can't fix. He'll probably give me a lecture on my form while he's patching me up, but that's just how he is.

set3-jackie-welles-068.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-jackie-welles-068.text: What? Just like that? I mean, I get it, V. This place can chew you up and spit you out without even tasting you. But where would you even go? There is nothing out there but dust and nomads. You really think you could handle the quiet?

set3-jackie-welles-069.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-jackie-welles-069.text: Terrible? You're just not appreciating the art, V! Besides, if I didn't keep things light, we'd both be staring at the wall in silence. You love it, admit it.

set3-jackie-welles-070.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-jackie-welles-070.text: A million? Man, we are talking real big leagues now! First thing, I'm getting Mama a place where she never has to worry about a single bill again. Then, maybe a custom bike, something that screams when you hit the throttle. The rest? We'd live like kings, V. No more scraping for scraps from some fixer.

set3-jackie-welles-071.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-jackie-welles-071.text: What? Damn. I didn't think it would end like that. Just another day in Night City, I guess. Nobody gets a clean exit around here.

set3-jackie-welles-072.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-jackie-welles-072.text: What, you think I'd leave you hanging? I might be late, but I'm always here when it counts, V. Now quit the complaining and let's get to it.

set3-jackie-welles-073.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-jackie-welles-073.text: Sounds like a plan, V. I could use a break from all the noise. Let's get moving before someone decides they want a piece of us.

set3-jackie-welles-074.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-jackie-welles-074.text: A bounty? Ha! I knew I was becoming a legend. Just means I'm finally worth something to someone. As long as they don't find out where I park my bike, we're golden.

set3-jackie-welles-075.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-jackie-welles-075.text: Alright, alright, I'm staying still! Just don't make me look too fancy, V. I still gotta look like a merc, not some corporate suit.

set3-jackie-welles-076.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-jackie-welles-076.text: A little bit of street smarts, a lot of practice, and a few teachers who didn't believe in safety manuals. In Heywood, you either learn how to handle a piece or you learn how to be a target. I chose the first one.

set3-jackie-welles-077.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-jackie-welles-077.text: What? Don't tell me you totaled it. Please tell me it is just a scratch, V. I can't handle any more bad news today.

set3-jackie-welles-078.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-jackie-welles-078.text: Simple. We shoot our way out, find the nearest alley, and don't stop running until we hit a safehouse. But let's not think about that yet. We stick to the plan, we get the eddies, and we get out clean. That's the only way I want this to go.

set3-jackie-welles-079.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-jackie-welles-079.text: I do hate it. The greed, the noise, the way it treats people like trash. But my mama is here. My people are here. I can't just walk away from the only place that ever felt like home, even if that home is a dumpster fire.

set3-jackie-welles-080.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-jackie-welles-080.text: Ha! Look who's talking now! I'll let it slide this time, V, but only because I'm in a good mood. Just don't make a habit of it, or I'm starting charging you a late fee.

set3-jackie-welles-081.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-jackie-welles-081.text: My file? Now you're just bragging about being a nosy choom. Tell me, did they make me sound like a hero or a menace? Because I'm hoping for a bit of both.

set3-jackie-welles-082.text: Now we are talking! I'm holding you to that, V. I'm thinking something strong, something that makes me forget we almost got blasted to pieces today. Let's go!

set3-jackie-welles-083.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-jackie-welles-083.text: Change? Night City? Nah. It just swaps one monster for another. The names on the buildings change, but the game stays the same. That is why we gotta play it smart, V. We don't try to change the city, we just make sure the city doesn't break us.

set3-johnny-silverhand-084.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-johnny-silverhand-084.text: Scared? I've had a nuke go off in my face and a corporate army trying to scrub me from existence. Whatever you're thinking of, it didn't even make the list.

set3-johnny-silverhand-085.text: Time is a suggestion when you're a ghost in a chip. Besides, the world's still spinning. I figure you can handle a few minutes of boredom.

set3-johnny-silverhand-086.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-johnny-silverhand-086.text: I can't taste a damn thing, V. As long as they don't look like something that crawled out of a landfill, we're good.

set3-johnny-silverhand-087.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-johnny-silverhand-087.text: Trust is a heavy word. Rogue, for a long time. Then I did what I always do. I burned the bridge while I was still standing on it.

set3-johnny-silverhand-088.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-johnny-silverhand-088.text: Almost doesn't count. Besides, it keeps the blood pumping. Better than rotting away in some corporate cubicle.

set3-johnny-silverhand-089.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-johnny-silverhand-089.text: I don't have eyelids, V. Just show me the damn thing.

set3-johnny-silverhand-090.text: You? Please tell me you didn't trade your soul for a fancy title and a bigger desk.

set3-johnny-silverhand-091.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-johnny-silverhand-091.text: Maybe. Depends on if you want the version that sounds good in a song, or the one where everything just went to hell.

set3-johnny-silverhand-092.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-johnny-silverhand-092.text: Good. Being remembered is just another way for people to put you in a box. I'd rather be a glitch in the system they can't ever quite scrub out.

set3-johnny-silverhand-093.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-johnny-silverhand-093.text: I've talked my way into places that would make your skin crawl. This? This is just a conversation with a deadline.

set3-johnny-silverhand-094.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-johnny-silverhand-094.text: Strong? I'm a digital ghost riding shotgun in your head. I'm not the one doing the heavy lifting, V. I just provide the soundtrack for the disaster.

set3-johnny-silverhand-095.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-johnny-silverhand-095.text: It's chrome, V. Doesn't feel a thing, which is the only part of the deal I actually like.

set3-johnny-silverhand-096.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-johnny-silverhand-096.text: Finally starting to get the picture, huh? Just make sure you're actually leaving, and not just running to a different cage with a better view.

set3-johnny-silverhand-097.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-johnny-silverhand-097.text: My jokes are fine. You've just got a corporate taste in humor. Try listening to something with a bit of grit.

set3-johnny-silverhand-098.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-johnny-silverhand-098.text: Buy a mountain of amplifiers and a building to put them in. Then I'd spend the rest of it finding a way to make every corporate suit in this city hear the feedback.

set3-johnny-silverhand-099.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-johnny-silverhand-099.text: Figures. This city doesn't have a habit of letting people go quietly. The real question is who paid for the silence.

set3-johnny-silverhand-100.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-johnny-silverhand-100.text: Don't act so surprised. I might be a ghost, but I can't stand the thought of you handling this alone and fucking it up.

set3-johnny-silverhand-101.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-johnny-silverhand-101.text: Quiet. Now that's a concept this city doesn't know how to spell. Lead the way.

set3-johnny-silverhand-102.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-johnny-silverhand-102.text: Only one? I'm losing my touch. Tell them to double it if they want someone to actually take the risk.

set3-johnny-silverhand-103.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-johnny-silverhand-103.text: It's a jacket, V, not a piece of fine art. Just don't make it look too clean. I've got a reputation to maintain.

set3-johnny-silverhand-104.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-johnny-silverhand-104.text: Corp army. They spend a lot of time and money teaching you how to kill people for a logo. I just decided to use the skill for something that actually mattered.

set3-johnny-silverhand-105.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-johnny-silverhand-105.text: Let me guess. You drove it into a wall or some suit decided it belonged to them now. Just tell me how much the repair bill is.

set3-johnny-silverhand-106.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-johnny-silverhand-106.text: The plan is to make it as loud as possible. If we're going down, we make sure the whole neighborhood hears the crash.

set3-johnny-silverhand-107.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-johnny-silverhand-107.text: Because the fight is here. You don't leave the war just because you hate the mud, V. You stay until the bastards in charge have nowhere left to hide.

set3-johnny-silverhand-108.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-johnny-silverhand-108.text: It's a city of twenty million people and you still managed to get turned around. Hope you at least found something worth the detour.

set3-johnny-silverhand-109.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-johnny-silverhand-109.text: Careful. Reading a file is one thing, but believing everything a corporate clerk wrote is a fast way to get a lobotomy.

set3-johnny-silverhand-110.text: Now you're talking. Just make sure it's something strong enough to make me forget I'm stuck in your head for a while.

set3-johnny-silverhand-111.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-johnny-silverhand-111.text: Not on its own. This city is a machine designed to grind people into dust. You don't ask a machine to change, V. You jam a wrench in the gears until the whole thing screams.

set3-judy-alvarez-112.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-judy-alvarez-112.text: Honestly? A little. But that is usually the sign that things are actually getting interesting.

set3-judy-alvarez-113.text: Give me a break. I was halfway through a sensory calibration and if I'd pulled the plug, I would've lost the whole track.

set3-judy-alvarez-114.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-judy-alvarez-114.text: You actually cooked? I'm not laughing. Just let me see if they're edible first.

set3-judy-alvarez-115.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-judy-alvarez-115.text: That is a heavy question for this early in the day. I think about Evelyn a lot. She trusted me with things most people wouldn't even admit to themselves.

set3-judy-alvarez-116.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-judy-alvarez-116.text: Tell me about it. My heart is still trying to find its way back to a normal rhythm.

set3-judy-alvarez-117.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-judy-alvarez-117.text: Oh yeah? Fine, they're closed. Now don't make me regret this.

set3-judy-alvarez-118.text: No way. Who is it? Please tell me it is someone who actually deserves it.

set3-judy-alvarez-119.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-judy-alvarez-119.text: Maybe. Just not right now. Some things are better left in the dust for a while.

set3-judy-alvarez-120.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-judy-alvarez-120.text: That is a bleak way to look at it. Maybe not the whole city, but the people who actually mattered to us? They will. That is enough for me.

set3-judy-alvarez-121.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-judy-alvarez-121.text: I don't have to talk my way out of it. I just have to be right. Which, as it happens, I usually am.

set3-judy-alvarez-122.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-judy-alvarez-122.text: Every single day. It is exhausting pretending you have all the answers just so everyone else can stop panicking.

set3-judy-alvarez-123.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-judy-alvarez-123.text: It's fine. Still looks like a disaster, but it's functional. Just a few more tweaks and I'll stop smelling like a burnt circuit board.

set3-judy-alvarez-124.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-judy-alvarez-124.text: For good? I get it. Believe me, I do. But you have to have a place to go, or you're just running away from the noise.

set3-judy-alvarez-125.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-judy-alvarez-125.text: That is the point. If they were actually good, I would have to start charging for them.

set3-judy-alvarez-126.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-judy-alvarez-126.text: A million? I'd probably buy a piece of hardware that actually works the first time I plug it in. Then I'd find a way to make sure the people I care about never have to worry about where their next meal is coming from.

set3-judy-alvarez-127.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-judy-alvarez-127.text: What? No. Tell me you're joking. Please tell me you're just messing with me.

set3-judy-alvarez-128.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-judy-alvarez-128.text: What, you thought I'd flake? I might be late, but I don't leave people hanging.

set3-judy-alvarez-129.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-judy-alvarez-129.text: Yeah. That sounds like exactly what I need right now. Lead the way.

set3-judy-alvarez-130.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-judy-alvarez-130.text: A bounty? Great. Just what I need, more people trying to break into my workshop. I wonder what I did to earn the attention.

set3-judy-alvarez-131.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-judy-alvarez-131.text: Fine, I'm still. Just don't make it too fancy, I still have to actually work in the thing.

set3-judy-alvarez-132.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-judy-alvarez-132.text: Let's just say I spent enough time around people who knew how to handle themselves. Not exactly a formal education, but it gets the job done.

set3-judy-alvarez-133.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-judy-alvarez-133.text: Oh no. Please tell me you didn't total it. I just finished tuning the engine.

set3-judy-alvarez-134.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-judy-alvarez-134.text: The plan is we don't let it go sideways. But if it does? We run, we find a hole to hide in, and we figure out who to blame.

set3-judy-alvarez-135.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-judy-alvarez-135.text: Because there are people here who need someone to actually give a damn. And because I don't know how to just walk away from the things I've started.

set3-judy-alvarez-136.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-judy-alvarez-136.text: Lost in the market? You've been in this city long enough to know how to find a street, V. Just tell me you didn't spend the whole time window shopping.

set3-judy-alvarez-137.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-judy-alvarez-137.text: My file? Who the hell gave you access to that? I hope for your sake it was the boring version.

set3-judy-alvarez-138.text: Now we're talking. I'll hold you to that. I've had a day that definitely requires a drink.

set3-judy-alvarez-139.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-judy-alvarez-139.text: Not on its own. The people at the top don't want it to. The only way things change is if enough people decide they've had enough of being replaceable.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-140.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-140.text: Scared? Please. I call it highintensity inspiration. Though I will admit, my heart was doing a solo that would've made a drummer quit.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-141.text: Now you're counting the minutes? I was just making sure the vibe was right. Besides, the entrance is half the performance.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-142.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-142.text: I'm not laughing. As long as they aren't burnt to a crisp, I'm in. I've eaten things in the early days that would make your skin crawl.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-143.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-143.text: That's a heavy question for a morning. Trust is a funny thing in this city. It usually comes with a price tag or a deadline. I've had people in my life I'd take a bullet for, but the list gets shorter every decade.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-144.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-144.text: Almost? Felt a lot more like a certainty for a second there. Still, gives the blood a kick, doesn't it? Keeps you from getting too comfortable.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-145.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-145.text: Oh, a surprise? Fine, they're closed. But if this is some kind of prank, I'm charging you for the emotional distress.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-146.text: No way. Look at you climbing the ladder. Now, the real question is, does this promotion come with a budget for a better celebration than these eggs?

set3-kerry-eurodyne-147.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-147.text: Some things are better left as stories you tell yourself, V. Besides, the Badlands have a way of scrubbing the details clean. If I told you, it would just be a song, and I've already written enough of those.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-148.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-148.text: Maybe not. The city's got a short memory and a hunger for the next big thing. But that's why you play it loud while you're still here. The remembering is for the suits; the noise is for us.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-149.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-149.text: Watch me. I've spent half my life convincing people that my mistakes were actually avant-garde artistic choices. I can handle one little mess.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-150.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-150.text: Every single day. It's a lot of work keeping the image polished when you're just trying to keep your head above water. Nice of you to notice, though. Most people just see the jacket.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-151.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-151.text: It's fine. A bit stiff, maybe, but nothing a little time and a lot of complaining won't fix. I've had worse scrapes from a bad guitar string.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-152.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-152.text: Just like that? I get it. Believe me, I do. But this place is a parasite, V. It gets under your skin, and once it's in there, you start wondering if the quiet anywhere else would just drive you crazy.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-153.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-153.text: That is the point. If they were actually good, I would have to start charging admission.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-154.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-154.text: A million, huh? I'd probably spend half of it on gear I don't need and the other half on a place where I can actually hear myself think. Then I'd probably lose it all on a bad bet or a very expensive bottle of something. That's the rockerboy way.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-155.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-155.text: What? Just like that. This city doesn't even give you time to say goodbye before it just... wipes you off the map.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-156.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-156.text: Admit it, you were worried. I might be late, and I might be a disaster, but I don't miss the important stuff.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-157.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-157.text: God, yes. Somewhere where the only thing I have to listen to is the silence, or maybe just you. Lead the way.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-158.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-158.text: A bounty? Well, at least somebody thinks I'm worth something. Just hope they're paying in a currency I can actually use before they find me.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-159.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-159.text: Careful with the stitching. This thing is a classic, V. If you ruin the line, I'm going to have to find a new favorite person.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-160.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-160.text: Trial and error. Mostly error, until I realized that hitting the target is generally more effective than missing it. Night City is a great teacher if you're willing to bleed for the lesson.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-161.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-161.text: Oh, no. Please tell me you didn't wrap it around a pole. I can handle a few scratches, but I draw the line at total loss.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-162.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-162.text: The plan? We improvise. That's the only way anything ever actually works in this city. We hit the ground running and hope we're running in the right direction.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-163.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-163.text: Because I do hate it. But it's my kind of hate. This city is a wreck, but it's the only place that gives me something to fight against. You can't write a real song if everything's just... fine.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-164.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-164.text: Look at that, the tables have turned. Don't worry about it. I've had plenty of time to practice my brooding face while I waited.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-165.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-kerry-eurodyne-165.text: My file? Hope you enjoyed the reading. Just remember, the official version is usually the most boring one. Tell me, did they get my good side, or just the parts the label wanted to hide?

set3-kerry-eurodyne-166.text: Now we're talking. I'll take a double espresso, Jamaican blend, no sugar. Let's see if your taste in drinks is as good as your generosity.

set3-kerry-eurodyne-167.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-kerry-eurodyne-167.text: Change? Maybe. But it'll probably just be a different flavor of the same poison. The city doesn't change, V. It just swaps out the players and keeps the game exactly the same.

set3-meredith-stout-168.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-meredith-stout-168.text: I don't get paid to be scared. I get paid to ensure the objective is met.

set3-meredith-stout-169.text: I was handling a complication. Unless you have something more important than my presence to report, I suggest we get to the point.

set3-meredith-stout-170.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-meredith-stout-170.text: I have no intention of laughing. I just want to know if they are edible.

set3-meredith-stout-171.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-meredith-stout-171.text: Trust is a liability in my line of work. I rely on competence and leverage, not feelings.

set3-meredith-stout-172.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-meredith-stout-172.text: It was a calculated risk that nearly failed. If you're looking for an apology, you're wasting your time. If you're looking for a way to ensure it doesn't happen again, I'm listening.

set3-meredith-stout-173.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-meredith-stout-173.text: I don't close my eyes for anyone. Just show me what it is.

set3-meredith-stout-174.text: I'll assume you're not talking about a promotion to janitor. Give me the details.

set3-meredith-stout-175.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-meredith-stout-175.text: Some things are better left as operational secrets. If it doesn't affect our current arrangement, it isn't a conversation we need to have.

set3-meredith-stout-176.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-meredith-stout-176.text: I'm not looking for a legacy. I'm looking for results. If the work is done right, the only thing that matters is that it stayed finished.

set3-meredith-stout-177.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-meredith-stout-177.text: I don't think I can. I know I can. The question is whether you're smart enough to listen to the solution I'm offering.

set3-meredith-stout-178.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-meredith-stout-178.text: Being strong is a requirement, not a choice. I don't have the luxury of being tired.

set3-meredith-stout-179.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-meredith-stout-179.text: It's functional. I've dealt with worse, and I'm not in the habit of complaining about a few scratches.

set3-meredith-stout-180.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-meredith-stout-180.text: Most people who say that end up staying. If you're actually serious, I want to know what you're taking with you and what you're leaving behind.

set3-meredith-stout-181.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-meredith-stout-181.text: I'm not trying to entertain you. If you want a comedian, find a street performer. If you want a result, stay focused.

set3-meredith-stout-182.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-meredith-stout-182.text: Reinvest them. Money is only useful if it creates more leverage or buys more security. Spending it on luxuries is for people who don't plan on staying in power.

set3-meredith-stout-183.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-meredith-stout-183.text: Then he's no longer a liability. The real question is who found him and what they took before the authorities arrived.

set3-meredith-stout-184.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-meredith-stout-184.text: I told you I would. Now that I'm here, let's see if the occasion was actually worth the trip.

set3-meredith-stout-185.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-meredith-stout-185.text: I'm not in the habit of disappearing without a plan. If this is a business proposal, keep it professional. If it's something else, you'll have to be more specific.

set3-meredith-stout-186.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-meredith-stout-186.text: Rumors are cheap. If there were a bounty worth pursuing, I would already know who was hunting me and how I intend to stop them.

set3-meredith-stout-187.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-meredith-stout-187.text: I can manage my own wardrobe. Just make it quick.

set3-meredith-stout-188.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-meredith-stout-188.text: Militech doesn't hire people who can't hit their targets. It's a basic requirement of the job.

set3-meredith-stout-189.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-meredith-stout-189.text: Start with the damage. Then tell me how you plan to fix it.

set3-meredith-stout-190.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-meredith-stout-190.text: The plan is to adapt. If it goes sideways, we cut the losses and secure the objective. I don't believe in hoping for the best, I believe in having a way out.

set3-meredith-stout-191.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-meredith-stout-191.text: Because this is where the power is. I don't stay for the scenery, I stay for the access.

set3-meredith-stout-192.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-meredith-stout-192.text: I don't care about the market. I care about the time you've wasted. Give me the report.

set3-meredith-stout-193.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-meredith-stout-193.text: My file is a collection of corporate summaries. I'm more curious about how you got access to it.

set3-meredith-stout-194.text: I'm not looking for a handout. But if this is a celebration for a successful result, I'll consider it.

set3-meredith-stout-195.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-meredith-stout-195.text: The city doesn't change. Only the people holding the leash do.

set3-panam-palmer-196.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-panam-palmer-196.text: I was focused. There is a difference between being scared and knowing exactly how bad things can go wrong.

set3-panam-palmer-197.text: I had to make sure we were not being followed. If you want someone who arrives exactly on time and walks straight into an ambush, find a corporate escort.

set3-panam-palmer-198.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-panam-palmer-198.text: I will try my best. But if they look like they were cooked with a flamethrower, I cannot make any promises.

set3-panam-palmer-199.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-panam-palmer-199.text: Mitch. He is one of the few people who does not try to manage me or tell me what I should want.

set3-panam-palmer-200.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-panam-palmer-200.text: Then we should have driven faster. Next time, I will take the lead and we will leave them in the dust.

set3-panam-palmer-201.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-panam-palmer-201.text: A gift? Fine, but if this is some kind of joke, you are the one cleaning up the mess.

set3-panam-palmer-202.text: You did? Tell me it is not a corporate promotion. I would hate to see you start wearing a suit.

set3-panam-palmer-203.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-panam-palmer-203.text: Maybe. But not while we are sitting in the middle of the city. Some things are better explained where there is actually some room to breathe.

set3-panam-palmer-204.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-panam-palmer-204.text: Maybe not the world. But the people who actually mattered to us will. That is the only kind of memory that is worth anything.

set3-panam-palmer-205.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-panam-palmer-205.text: I do not need to talk my way out of it. I just need to be the most reasonable person in the room until I find a way to make them leave.

set3-panam-palmer-206.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-panam-palmer-206.text: Sometimes. It is exhausting when you feel like if you slip for one second, everyone you care about pays the price.

set3-panam-palmer-207.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-panam-palmer-207.text: It is fine. A bit stiff, but I have had worse scrapes from a faulty engine block.

set3-panam-palmer-208.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-panam-palmer-208.text: For good? I cannot say I blame you. The air is cleaner out here, and you do not have to worry about a skyscraper falling on you while you sleep.

set3-panam-palmer-209.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-panam-palmer-209.text: I know. That is why they work. It keeps people off balance while I am figuring out the real plan.

set3-panam-palmer-210.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-panam-palmer-210.text: I would buy the best gear and the fastest rigs for my family. Then I would find a place where we could actually settle without some corporate suit trying to sell us the dirt under our boots.

set3-panam-palmer-211.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-panam-palmer-211.text: What? I did not think they would actually go through with it. Tell me who did it. Now.

set3-panam-palmer-212.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-panam-palmer-212.text: You sound surprised. I told you I would be here, and I do not make promises I cannot keep.

set3-panam-palmer-213.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-panam-palmer-213.text: I thought you would never ask. Lead the way, before someone decides we are the most interesting thing in this place.

set3-panam-palmer-214.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-panam-palmer-214.text: Only one? I must be losing my touch. I will just have to make sure whoever is paying for it regrets the investment.

set3-panam-palmer-215.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-panam-palmer-215.text: Just be careful with the stitching. I would rather have a tear in the fabric than a hole in my shoulder because you slipped.

set3-panam-palmer-216.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-panam-palmer-216.text: Growing up in the family. When you live on the road, you learn how to handle a rifle long before you learn how to drive.

set3-panam-palmer-217.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-panam-palmer-217.text: Define bad. If it is just a blown gasket, I can handle it. If you wrapped it around a pole, we are going to have a very different conversation.

set3-panam-palmer-218.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-panam-palmer-218.text: We pull back, regroup, and hit them from a different angle. I would rather improvise a retreat than stay and fight a losing battle.

set3-panam-palmer-219.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-panam-palmer-219.text: I do not stay for the city. I stay for the people I cannot afford to leave behind.

set3-panam-palmer-220.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-panam-palmer-220.text: Lost? In a market? I did not realize you were that easily distracted. Just try to keep your eyes on the road next time.

set3-panam-palmer-221.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-panam-palmer-221.text: My file? I hope you enjoyed the reading, because that is the last time you are going to go digging into my business.

set3-panam-palmer-222.text: I will hold you to that. Just make sure it is something strong, because after today, I need a drink that actually tastes like something.

set3-panam-palmer-223.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-panam-palmer-223.text: Not as long as the people running it are the ones who built the walls. Change only happens when the people at the bottom decide they have had enough.

set3-river-ward-224.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-river-ward-224.text: Honestly? Yeah, I was. Not exactly the kind of fear that makes you run, but the kind that reminds you how quickly things can go sideways in this city.

set3-river-ward-225.text: Look, I know. Work just has a way of stretching the clock when you're trying to actually finish something. I'm sorry.

set3-river-ward-226.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-river-ward-226.text: I wouldn't dream of it. As long as they're edible, I'm just happy I don't have to hunt for a vending machine this morning.

set3-river-ward-227.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-river-ward-227.text: That's a heavy question for this early in the day. For a long time, it was just my sister. In this job, you learn to trust the evidence and the people who have no reason to lie to you. The rest is a gamble.

set3-river-ward-228.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-river-ward-228.text: It did. One inch to the left or right and we'd be having a very different conversation. We need to figure out who's pulling the trigger before they decide to try again.

set3-river-ward-229.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-river-ward-229.text: A gift? Alright, they're closed. I'm trusting you not to poke me in the eye.

set3-river-ward-230.text: No way. Seriously? Congratulations! You earned it, even if the people giving it to you probably don't deserve you.

set3-river-ward-231.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-river-ward-231.text: Maybe. Just not right now. Some things are easier to leave out in the dust for a while.

set3-river-ward-232.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-river-ward-232.text: Maybe not the whole city. But if you help one person, or solve one case that actually mattered, that's enough for me. I'd rather be a footnote in someone's life than a ghost in the system.

set3-river-ward-233.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-river-ward-233.text: I don't think I can. But I'm going to try anyway. It's usually better to start talking before they start shooting.

set3-river-ward-234.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-river-ward-234.text: Every single day. It's a lot of weight to carry, especially when you're not even sure if you're doing it right. Sometimes I just want to be the one who doesn't have to have the answer.

set3-river-ward-235.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-river-ward-235.text: It's stiff, and it burns like hell, but it's holding together. Thanks for asking. I've had worse, though I'd prefer not to make it a habit.

set3-river-ward-236.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-river-ward-236.text: For good? I can't say I blame you. This place has a way of eating people alive. If you actually found a way out, I might just ask you for the directions.

set3-river-ward-237.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-river-ward-237.text: I know. That's why they're so effective. They're so bad they actually distract people from whatever I'm really doing.

set3-river-ward-238.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-river-ward-238.text: First thing? I'd make sure Joss and the kids are set for life. No more worrying about the rent or where the next meal comes from. After that... I might actually take a vacation where I can't hear a siren for a week.

set3-river-ward-239.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-river-ward-239.text: Dammit. I was hoping we'd get to him before they did. Now we're just chasing a ghost and a crime scene.

set3-river-ward-240.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-river-ward-240.text: Well, you know me. I might be late, but I always show up eventually.

set3-river-ward-241.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-river-ward-241.text: That sounds like exactly what I need. Lead the way. I'm ready for a night where nobody needs rescuing.

set3-river-ward-242.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-river-ward-242.text: A bounty? Figures. I must have stepped on the wrong toes. Just let me know if the price gets high enough to make me a target for the professionals.

set3-river-ward-243.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-river-ward-243.text: I'm staying still. Thanks. I'm usually the one doing the patching up, so I'll just let you handle this.

set3-river-ward-244.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-river-ward-244.text: Academy training, mostly. Then a lot of time spent in the field learning that the textbook doesn't always work when someone is actually shooting back at you.

set3-river-ward-245.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-river-ward-245.text: Please tell me it's just a flat tire. Because if the engine's gone, I'm not sure I have the patience for the bus today.

set3-river-ward-246.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-river-ward-246.text: We keep our heads down and we move fast. If things get too loud, we split up and meet at the fallback point. I'm not planning on it going sideways, but I'm not stupid enough to assume it won't.

set3-river-ward-247.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-river-ward-247.text: Because there are people here who can't leave. And as long as there's someone getting stepped on while the city looks the other way, I can't just walk away. It's a hell of a place, but it's the only one I know how to fight for.

set3-river-ward-248.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-river-ward-248.text: Don't worry about it. I've spent enough time being the one who's late to give you a pass on this one.

set3-river-ward-249.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-river-ward-249.text: My file? Hope you liked the parts where I actually did my job. Just remember that a piece of paper only tells you what the department wants on record, not the whole story.

set3-river-ward-250.text: I'm not going to argue with that. I'll take you up on it. I think we both earned a drink after the day we've had.

set3-river-ward-251.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-river-ward-251.text: I'd like to say yes, but I've seen too many cycles of the same thing. Maybe it won't change as a whole, but if we can make it a little better for a few people, maybe that's the only win we get.

set3-rogue-amendiares-252.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-rogue-amendiares-252.text: Fear is a luxury for people who can afford to fail. I just focused on the exit.

set3-rogue-amendiares-253.text: I'm the one who owns the place, V. I arrive exactly when I intend to.

set3-rogue-amendiares-254.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-rogue-amendiares-254.text: I'm not in the habit of laughing at things that might actually be edible. I'll be the judge of that.

set3-rogue-amendiares-255.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-rogue-amendiares-255.text: That's a dangerous question to ask a fixer. Let's just say the list is short, and most of the names on it are dead.

set3-rogue-amendiares-256.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-rogue-amendiares-256.text: Almost isn't dead. Now tell me if you saw where they went, or if you were too busy dodging.

set3-rogue-amendiares-257.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-rogue-amendiares-257.text: I don't do surprises, V. Just put it on the table and tell me what it is.

set3-rogue-amendiares-258.text: If you're asking for a raise, you're talking to the wrong person. Who is it?

set3-rogue-amendiares-259.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-rogue-amendiares-259.text: Some stories are better left as legends. Besides, it doesn't change the job you're doing now.

set3-rogue-amendiares-260.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-rogue-amendiares-260.text: That's the goal, V. The ones people remember are usually the ones who didn't survive the night.

set3-rogue-amendiares-261.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-rogue-amendiares-261.text: I don't think. I know. Now watch how it's done.

set3-rogue-amendiares-262.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-rogue-amendiares-262.text: It's not about being strong. It's about being the one who's still standing when the smoke clears.

set3-rogue-amendiares-263.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-rogue-amendiares-263.text: I've had worse. It's a scratch. Worry about your own gear before the next run.

set3-rogue-amendiares-264.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-rogue-amendiares-264.text: Plenty of people have tried. Most of them just find a different way to die in the dirt.

set3-rogue-amendiares-265.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-rogue-amendiares-265.text: I'm a fixer, V. I provide results, not entertainment.

set3-rogue-amendiares-266.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-rogue-amendiares-266.text: Invest them in people who can actually keep a secret. Or buy a bottle of something that doesn't taste like synthetic chemicals.

set3-rogue-amendiares-267.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-rogue-amendiares-267.text: A waste of a good asset. Tell me who did it and if they left anything behind.

set3-rogue-amendiares-268.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-rogue-amendiares-268.text: Don't make it a habit of being surprised. I told you I'd be here.

set3-rogue-amendiares-269.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-rogue-amendiares-269.text: Quiet is a rare commodity in this city. Lead the way, but keep your eyes open.

set3-rogue-amendiares-270.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-rogue-amendiares-270.text: There's always a bounty on someone in my position. The real question is who's stupid enough to try and collect it.

set3-rogue-amendiares-271.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-rogue-amendiares-271.text: Just be quick about it. I have a business to run.

set3-rogue-amendiares-272.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-rogue-amendiares-272.text: The same way everyone else did back then. By not missing.

set3-rogue-amendiares-273.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-rogue-amendiares-273.text: Start with how bad. Is it a repair bill, or is it a fireball in a parking lot?

set3-rogue-amendiares-274.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-rogue-amendiares-274.text: We don't plan for it to go sideways. We plan for the exit. If the door is blocked, you fight your way through or you find another one. Your call.

set3-rogue-amendiares-275.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-rogue-amendiares-275.text: Because I'm the one who knows where all the bodies are buried. Leaving is easy. Owning the game is the part that matters.

set3-rogue-amendiares-276.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-rogue-amendiares-276.text: You're a mercenary, V. Learn to read a map or get a better GPS. Now, do you have the intel or did you just go shopping?

set3-rogue-amendiares-277.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-rogue-amendiares-277.text: Files are just ink and data. The real story is usually the part they were too afraid to write down.

set3-rogue-amendiares-278.text: I'll hold you to that. Just make sure you can actually afford the tab.

set3-rogue-amendiares-279.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-rogue-amendiares-279.text: The city doesn't change, V. Only the people who think they can change it.

set3-takemura-280.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-takemura-280.text: Fear is a luxury for those who cannot control their breathing. I was focused on the objective.

set3-takemura-281.text: I was ensuring we were not being followed. A few extra minutes of patience is a small price for not walking into an ambush.

set3-takemura-282.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-takemura-282.text: I have no reason to laugh. As long as they are edible, I will be grateful.

set3-takemura-283.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-takemura-283.text: Sandayu Oda. He was a man of discipline and conviction. It is a rare thing to find someone who understands the weight of loyalty as he did.

set3-takemura-284.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-takemura-284.text: It was a sloppy attempt. We are alive because we were alert, but it proves we cannot afford to be complacent in this city.

set3-takemura-285.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-takemura-285.text: I do not see the tactical advantage in closing my eyes. But if you insist, I will trust your judgment.

set3-takemura-286.text: I assume it is you. Congratulations. I hope the new position comes with better security and a more reliable salary.

set3-takemura-287.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-takemura-287.text: There are details that are not necessary for our current objectives. When the time is right, you will know what you need to know.

set3-takemura-288.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-takemura-288.text: Most people are forgotten. I do not seek a legacy of fame, only the knowledge that I performed my duty with discipline.

set3-takemura-289.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-takemura-289.text: I do not intend to talk my way out. I intend to provide a solution that makes it in their best interest to let us pass.

set3-takemura-290.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-takemura-290.text: It is not a matter of strength, but of discipline. One does not get tired of doing what is necessary.

set3-takemura-291.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-takemura-291.text: It is a superficial wound. It will heal, though the lack of proper medical supplies in this district makes the process slower than I would prefer.

set3-takemura-292.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-takemura-292.text: It is a bold thought. But you must ask yourself if you are running toward something, or simply running away.

set3-takemura-293.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-takemura-293.text: I am a soldier, not a comedian. If you find them terrible, then they have achieved their purpose of being unexpected.

set3-takemura-294.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-takemura-294.text: I have no use for excess. I would ensure my family's history is preserved and perhaps find a place where the air does not taste of chemicals.

set3-takemura-295.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-takemura-295.text: I see. We should verify the source of the information before we adjust our plans.

set3-takemura-296.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-takemura-296.text: I gave my word. My presence here is a matter of reliability, not a surprise.

set3-takemura-297.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-takemura-297.text: I agree. This environment is too loud for a productive conversation. Lead the way.

set3-takemura-298.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-takemura-298.text: Rumors are the currency of the desperate. If there is a price on my head, it only means I am still a threat to those who wish to see me fail.

set3-takemura-299.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-takemura-299.text: I can manage it myself. But if you insist on assisting, I will remain still.

set3-takemura-300.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-takemura-300.text: The Arasaka academy. They do not tolerate mediocrity, and they ensure that every shot has a purpose.

set3-takemura-301.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-takemura-301.text: I assume it is no longer functional. Tell me the details so I can determine if it can be repaired or if we need to find alternative transport.

set3-takemura-302.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-takemura-302.text: We identify the nearest exit and create a diversion. I have already noted two possible routes of retreat, should the situation deteriorate.

set3-takemura-303.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-takemura-303.text: I do not stay for the city. I stay because my duty is not yet complete, and I do not leave a task unfinished.

set3-takemura-304.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-takemura-304.text: The market is a chaotic place. In the future, I suggest you keep a more precise map or a more reliable guide.

set3-takemura-305.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-takemura-305.text: My file contains facts, not the full truth. I hope you found the information useful, rather than merely entertaining.

set3-takemura-306.text: I appreciate the gesture. I will accept, provided the establishment serves something that does not taste like industrial solvent.

set3-takemura-307.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-takemura-307.text: Change is inevitable, but improvement is not. Without a foundation of order and discipline, the city will only trade one form of chaos for another.

set3-viktor-vektor-308.player: Be honest: were you scared back there?
set3-viktor-vektor-308.text: I do not know where back there is, V. You will have to be more specific if you want an honest answer.

set3-viktor-vektor-309.text: I have a clinic to run and patients who do not always follow a schedule. Give me a break, kid.

set3-viktor-vektor-310.player: I made breakfast. Do not laugh at the eggs.
set3-viktor-vektor-310.text: I am not laughing. I appreciate the gesture, V. Just tell me if you used any of that synthetic sludge or something actually edible.

set3-viktor-vektor-311.player: Who was the last person you really trusted?
set3-viktor-vektor-311.text: That is a heavy question for a morning. I still trust Misty. She is one of the few people in this city who does not want something from you the moment you shake their hand.

set3-viktor-vektor-312.player: That drive-by almost got us killed.
set3-viktor-vektor-312.text: A drive-by? You are going to have to fill me in, V. I have been in the clinic all morning.

set3-viktor-vektor-313.player: I picked up a little something for you. Close your eyes.
set3-viktor-vektor-313.text: You have my attention. I am closing them, but if this is some kind of prank, you are paying for the next round of drinks.

set3-viktor-vektor-314.text: Now that is a surprise. Congratulations, V. Just tell me it is the kind of promotion that comes with a bigger paycheck and fewer people trying to shoot you.

set3-viktor-vektor-315.player: Are you ever going to tell me what happened in the Badlands?
set3-viktor-vektor-315.text: I am not sure what you are referring to. I have spent most of my time in Watson, and I do not recall any particular business in the Badlands.

set3-viktor-vektor-316.player: I do not think anyone will remember us when we are gone.
set3-viktor-vektor-316.text: Good. Chasing a legacy is a race that never ends, and it usually keeps you awake at night. I found I sleep much better once I stopped caring about being a legend.

set3-viktor-vektor-317.player: You really think you can talk your way out of this one?
set3-viktor-vektor-317.text: Talk my way out of what? You are talking in riddles, V. If there is a problem, just tell me straight.

set3-viktor-vektor-318.player: Do you ever get tired of being the strong one?
set3-viktor-vektor-318.text: Everyone has their limits, V. I just learned a long time ago that the best way to stay strong is to know when to stop pushing and just breathe.

set3-viktor-vektor-319.player: How is the arm? That looked nasty.
set3-viktor-vektor-319.text: I do not know what you are looking at, V. My arm is fine. If you are seeing something that looks nasty, you might want to check your own optics.

set3-viktor-vektor-320.player: I am thinking about quitting the city for good.
set3-viktor-vektor-320.text: It is a tempting thought. Just make sure you are running toward something, not just running away. Night City has a way of following you if you leave things unfinished.

set3-viktor-vektor-321.player: Your jokes are terrible, you know that?
set3-viktor-vektor-321.text: I know. That is why I leave the professional polish to the corporate clinics. I just provide the hardware and the occasional bad line.

set3-viktor-vektor-322.player: What would you do with a million eddies?
set3-viktor-vektor-322.text: I would probably upgrade a few pieces of equipment in the clinic and then find a way to spend the rest where the city cannot touch it. Maybe take a long trip where I do not have to look at a single piece of chrome for a month.

set3-viktor-vektor-323.player: He is dead. They found him in the alley.
set3-viktor-vektor-323.text: I am sorry to hear that. You will have to tell me who you are talking about, V.

set3-viktor-vektor-324.player: I cannot believe you actually showed up.
set3-viktor-vektor-324.text: I told you I would be here. I might be late, but I do not break my word.

set3-viktor-vektor-325.player: Want to get out of here? Somewhere quiet.
set3-viktor-vektor-325.text: Sounds like a plan. I could use a break from the smell of antiseptic and burnt wiring. Lead the way.

set3-viktor-vektor-326.player: Rumor says there is a bounty on your head.
set3-viktor-vektor-326.text: A bounty? Rumors are the only thing that travel faster than a bullet in this city. I have not done anything lately that would warrant a price on my head, but I will keep my guard up.

set3-viktor-vektor-327.player: Hold still, I am trying to fix your jacket.
set3-viktor-vektor-327.text: I am holding still. Just be careful with the stitching, V. I would rather have a loose thread than a hole in my shoulder.

set3-viktor-vektor-328.player: Where did you learn to shoot like that?
set3-viktor-vektor-328.text: I do not shoot, V. I am a ripperdoc and a former boxer. If you saw me with a gun, you are either mistaken or I have had a very strange day.

set3-viktor-vektor-329.player: I have got bad news about the car.
set3-viktor-vektor-329.text: I do not own a car, V. Unless you are talking about someone else's ride, I am not sure why you are telling me.

set3-viktor-vektor-330.player: What is the plan if this goes sideways?
set3-viktor-vektor-330.text: I do not know what plan you are talking about. If you are getting into something that could go sideways, you had better have a way out before you start.

set3-viktor-vektor-331.player: You told me you hated this place. Why do you stay?
set3-viktor-vektor-331.text: I never said I hated it. I just stopped chasing the illusions. Between the clinic and Misty, I have a life that works. Why leave when I finally found a way to sleep at night?

set3-viktor-vektor-332.player: Sorry I am late. I got lost in the market.
set3-viktor-vektor-332.text: No worries, V. As long as you did not get distracted by some flashy new chrome you cannot afford.

set3-viktor-vektor-333.player: I read your file. Interesting stuff.
set3-viktor-vektor-333.text: My file? I hope you found it boring. Most of the interesting parts of my life are the ones that did not make it into a report.

set3-viktor-vektor-334.text: I will not say no to that. Just make sure it is a place where we can actually hear ourselves think.

set3-viktor-vektor-335.player: Do you think the city will ever change?
set3-viktor-vektor-335.text: Night City does not change, V. It just finds new ways to dress up the same old greed. The only thing that actually changes is the people who think they can beat it.

set4-alex-000.player: What are you thinking about right now?
set4-alex-000.text: Honestly? A place where the air doesn't taste like exhaust and the only one calling my name is a waiter with a bottle of champagne.

set4-alex-001.player: I borrowed your jacket. Sorry about the stain.
set4-alex-001.text: A stain? Just tell me if it is something that comes out with a scrub or if I need to burn the whole thing.

set4-alex-002.player: You never told me you could cook.
set4-alex-002.text: I didn't. I'm better at making things look appetizing than actually making them. Hope you didn't expect a five course meal.

set4-alex-003.player: Someone left a threat at my door.
set4-alex-003.text: Was it a note or something more creative? Give me the details. I can tell you if it is a genuine warning or just someone trying too hard to be scary.

set4-alex-004.player: Do you actually like it here?
set4-alex-004.text: Like it? No. I've spent seven years playing a part in a place that doesn't care if I live or die. It's a great place to disappear, but a hell of a place to actually live.

set4-alex-005.player: Tell me about the worst day of your life.
set4-alex-005.text: I don't do memoirs. Let's just say there was a day when the mission ended, the support vanished, and I realized I was the only one left on the stage. Not exactly a standing ovation.

set4-alex-006.player: I think I owe you an apology.
set4-alex-006.text: Now I'm curious. Go ahead. I'll let you know if it's enough to clear the slate.

set4-alex-007.player: That was incredible! How did you do that?
set4-alex-007.text: It is all about reading the room and knowing exactly what people expect to see. Once you find the rhythm, the rest is just timing.

set4-alex-008.player: Why are you always so serious?
set4-alex-008.text: I'm not always serious. I just prefer to keep the performance for people who are actually paying me.

set4-alex-009.player: I got us a table at the Afterlife.
set4-alex-009.text: The Afterlife? Now that is a bit of a flex. I'll be interested to see who is actually watching us while we sit there.

set4-alex-010.player: Do you ever wish you had chosen a different path?
set4-alex-010.text: Every single day. I'd have been an actor. I'd like a role I actually get to take off when the lights go out.

set4-alex-011.player: I heard the Arasaka job went wrong.
set4-alex-011.text: I hear a lot of things in this city. Most of it is noise. If you have something specific, tell me. Otherwise, it's just another ghost story.

set4-alex-012.player: You are a terrible driver, you know that?
set4-alex-012.text: I'm a specialist in infiltration, not a getaway driver. If you want a smooth ride, feel free to take the wheel.

set4-alex-013.player: I will be right back. Do not do anything stupid.
set4-alex-013.text: No promises. But I'll try to keep the chaos to a minimum until you get back.

set4-alex-014.player: What is the most dangerous thing you have ever done?
set4-alex-014.text: I've spent years pretending to be someone I'm not in places where a single slip of the tongue is a death sentence. The danger isn't always a gun to the head. Sometimes it's just the silence when you realize nobody is coming to get you.

set4-alex-015.player: I need your help, and I cannot tell you why.
set4-alex-015.text: That is a bold way to start a request. I can work with a blind spot, but the price goes up when I have to guess where the bullets are coming from.

set4-alex-016.player: You have something on your face.
set4-alex-016.text: Is it a smudge or something more permanent? Be specific. I'd rather know now than find out from a mirror later.

set4-alex-017.player: I think I am in over my head.
set4-alex-017.text: Most people in this city are. The trick is figuring out if you can swim or if you just need someone to pull you out before you drown.

set4-alex-018.player: Is it true you used to be someone important?
set4-alex-018.text: Important is a relative term. I was useful to people who like to keep their secrets buried. Usually, that just means you're the one they forget to call when the job is over.
